stories.title: Administrators to replace Pradhans till UP Panchayat polls for 1st-time:No major decisions allowed; proposals need DM approval through DPRO
stories.summary: In UP, either panchayat elections will be held, or the Gram Pradhan will remain as administrator for the next 6 months. After getting the green signal from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Principal Secretary of the Panchayati Raj Department Anil Kumar issued orders late Monday evening. The Principal Secretary has assigned the responsibility of appointing Pradhans as administrators to the District Magistrates. According to the order, the administrator, i.e. Gram Pradhan, will not be able to take any major or policy-related decision at their level. If it becomes necessary to take such a decision in any urgent or special situation, then its proposal will be sent to the District Magistrate through the District Panchayati Raj Officer. Action will be taken on it only after getting approval from the District Magistrate. Same arrangement may be made for Block Pramukh - District Panchayat President as well The term of all 57,694 gram panchayats in UP is ending on Tuesday (26 May). Panchayat elections will be held only after the 2027 Assembly elections. It is believed that when the term of the Block Pramukh and District Panchayat President ends in July, an administrative committee will be formed under the chairmanship of the Block Pramukh at the block level and the District Panchayat President at the district level. Panchayati Raj Minister Omprakash Rajbhar said, The term of Gram Pradhans will end on 26 May. The government has decided to appoint administrators, now the Gram Pradhans themselves will work as administrators until the three-tier panchayat elections are held. Till now, the tradition has been to make ADO the administrator In 2021, as well, panchayat elections were held about 3 months later than their scheduled time. Actually, in 2015, panchayat elections were conducted between October and December. After this, the first meeting of newly elected gram pradhans was held on January 26, 2016. According to this, the tenure of pradhans was ending on January 26, 2021. However, due to the COVID pandemic and voter list verification not being completed on time, panchayat elections were held in four phases in April 2021. For a period of three months, an Assistant Development Officer (ADO) or a Block Development Officer (BDO) was appointed as administrator. Whereas in the year 2000, panchayat elections were held about 2 months late. Even then, officers were made administrators. This time, the Yogi government has made arrangements to give responsibility to gram pradhans themselves, following the pattern of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Why is an administrative committee being formed? 1. The final publication of the voter list for panchayat elections has not yet taken place. The tenure of Gram Pradhans is until May 26, while the final publication of the list will be on June 10. 2. The proposal to form an OBC Commission to determine OBC reservation in panchayat elections has been approved by the Cabinet. The commission will submit its report within 3 to 6 months of its formation. After that, reservations for elections will be determined. This may take 6 months. 3. The government is considering conducting panchayat elections after the Assembly elections. Political parties have also agreed in principle, but the matter is pending in the Allahabad High Court. Why did the government make Pradhans administrators? In assembly elections, for assembly seats in rural areas, the Gram Pradhan is the first and most important link for any political party. The responsibility of winning elections, increasing vote percentage, managing booths, conducting election campaigns, and gathering crowds at rallies also rests with them. If an employee were appointed as administrator, the outgoing Gram Pradhan would not be as effective. They would not prove to be as helpful for the ruling party either. At the same time, development work in villages before elections and the implementation of government schemes would also be affected. Therefore, the government has taken a well-considered decision to appoint the Gram Pradhan itself as administrator. Pradhan Sangh had also demanded formation of 'Administrative Committee' The National Panchayati Raj Gram Pradhan Sangathan's National President, Akhilesh Singh, had spoken to Dainik Bhaskar on this subject. He had said that the organisation's delegation met CM Yogi on April 20 and demanded the formation of an administrative committee. On May 16, they met with the BJP's State President, Pankaj Chaudhary and placed the same demand before him. The organisation's Vice President Lalit Kumar Sharma had informed that if panchayat elections are not held on time, the state government or district magistrate can form an administrator or administrative committee. This is done under Section 12, Sub-section 3A of the Panchayati Raj Act 1947. The administrative committee has the Gram Pradhan or a chairman designated by the government. Meanwhile, the Gram Pradhan, along with ward members of the panchayat and the Gram Panchayat assistant, are made members. Difficulties arise from appointing administrators National President of the Pradhan Sangh, Akhilesh Singh, had stated that appointing government employees as administrators in Gram Panchayats creates various problems for villagers. Pradhan organisation expressed happiness The National Panchayati Raj Gram Pradhan Organisation has expressed happiness over Pradhans being made administrators for the first time. The national president of the organisation, Dr. Akhilesh Singh, has said that the government has given a gift to the Pradhans, and the Pradhans will give a return gift in the assembly elections. He said that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had made a promise to the Pradhans on December 15, 2021, at the Gram Utkarsh Samaroh to form a triple-engine government, which he has fulfilled. The gift of expansion of services that he has given, the Gram Pradhans will return this gift to the Chief Minister in 2027. The Pradhan organisation will express gratitude by organising ceremonies at the state, division, district and block levels.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visits Taj Mahal with wife; Fuel prices hiked for 4th time in 12 days more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. CM Yogi attends Prateek Yadav's 'terawi' ceremony The ‘tehravi’ ceremony of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s brother Prateek Yadav was held on Monday. During the programme, Prateek’s wife, Aparna Yadav, distributed pooris among attendees. 2. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visits Taj Mahal with wife US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited the Taj Mahal with his wife Jeanette Rubio on Monday morning. The couple reached the monument at around 10:15 am. 3. Fuel prices hiked again, 4th time in 12 days Oil companies have once again increased petrol and diesel prices, marking the fourth fuel price hike this month. Petrol prices have gone up by ₹2.61 per litre, while diesel has become costlier by ₹2.71 per litre. After the latest revision, petrol in Delhi is now priced at ₹102.12 per litre, while diesel costs ₹95.20 per litre. 4. Premanand Ji appeal devotees to focus on Shri Ji Premanand Maharaj has issued an emotional appeal to his disciples and devotees through a video message released from Vrindavan. The 1-minute-19-second video was uploaded on Sunday on the official YouTube channel of Kelly Kunj Ashram Trust. 5. SC questions NTA; says no lesson learnt from previous NEET leak The Supreme Court on Monday, May 25, expressed concern over the National Testing Agency’s (NTA) handling of the NEET examination process, observing that it was ‘sad’ the agency appeared not to have learned lessons from previous paper leak controversies. 6. Shankaracharya to buy cows through ‘Go-LX' app Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati is set to launch the Go-LX app as part of his cow protection campaign. Speaking during his ongoing cow protection yatra, the Shankaracharya said the platform would only facilitate the ‘purchase’ of cows, not their sale. 7. Dharmendra gets Padma Vibhushan posthumously, received by Hema Malini Padma Awards are being presented at Rashtrapati Bhavan on Monday. President Droupadi Murmu first conferred the Padma Vibhushan on late film star Dharmendra. His wife, actor-MP Hema Malini, received the honour on his behalf. 8. Child dies falls from zip line after safety belt open A 15-year-old son of a bangle businessman died after falling from a 45-foot-high zip line in Agra. A video of the incident has also surfaced. The footage shows that as the teenager moved towards the other end of the zip line, the hook attached to his safety belt came loose, causing him to fall. 9. How big is power crisis in UP? On one hand, temperatures in Uttar Pradesh are touching new highs every day. On the other, power cuts from cities to villages have triggered widespread public anger. stories.title: 5 arrested with fake notes in Gorakhpur:All had formed gang, would make 400 rupee notes in exchange for 100
stories.summary: Gorakhpur's Gulriha police have arrested 5 men on Monday with counterfeit notes. During interrogation, the accused revealed that they had started the business of making fake notes. They would make 400 rupees in exchange for 100 rupees. They would guarantee to circulate those fake notes in any market. The arrested accused were identified as Karan Singh from Padri Bazar New Christian Colony in Shahpur, Mohit Kumar resident of Bargadwa in Gorakhnath area, Vishal Sharma from Padri Bazar, Ashish Sharma from Mohanpur, and Akash Singh resident of Bhalui Pipra Tola in Ahirauli police station area of Kushinagar. According to police, Mohit Kumar Paswan is a lawyer at the Civil Court. Akash Singh runs a medical store. Vishal runs a printing press where Ashish Sharma works. All the accused are also friends with each other. Police recovered from them 09 fake notes of 500 rupees, 01 fake note of 100 rupees, 04 mobiles and 1 Apple mobile, monitor, CPU, keyboard, mouse, 2 printers, 4 ink bottles, 01 bundle of A4 size paper, 49 various types of printed A4 size fake note forms, 14 double-sided printed fake notes, 02 wires used in notes, 04 forms with Gandhiji's photo, 39 bundles of black colored printed/plain paper of 500 rupee size. This is how the arrest was made SP City Nimish Patil, while holding a press conference at the White House, informed that the Gulriha police station was checking suspicious vehicles and persons. Just then, information was received from a special informer that some persons were engaged in preparing fake notes in a shutter-like shop located in Saraswatipuram Colony, Padri Bazar. On this information, Gulriha police, SOG team and Surveillance Cell team immediately reached the spot with force. While cordoning off the area, the persons involved in making fake notes were caught. In this case, the name of a person from Bihar has also come up. The police are finding out about him. He has also been made an accused in this case.

stories.title: Russian vlogger and dog lover rebukes Indian in Varanasi:Natasha was upset over man when he crushed puppy's leg, gets 100 animals dressed up
stories.summary: A Russian woman got furious at a young man and hurled abuses at him in Varanasi city. During this, she was holding a puppy (baby dog) in her hand. She started shouting angrily, "You broke this puppy's leg, now why are you laughing?" The video of this incident that occurred on Sunday surfaced on Monday. It shows the Russian woman standing in the lane leading to Narad Ghat with a puppy in her lap. She is hurling abuses at the young man right there. She is accusing him of breaking the puppy's leg. During this, a large number of people gathered. The woman is Pink Natasha, a content creator and animal rescuer from Russia. First 2 pictures... Know what is shown in the video In a narrow lane leading to Narad Ghat, Pink Natasha is standing holding an injured puppy in her arms. One leg of the puppy is badly injured. Blood is flowing from it. The Russian woman shows the puppy's leg to all the people present there. Natasha accuses the young man saying he had harmed a voiceless animal. Then the young man also says something to Natasha. At this, Natasha gets angry and starts abusing. During the incident, some people standing around keep laughing. At this, Natasha becomes even more angry. Now know who is Pink Natasha? Pink Natasha is a well-known Russian vlogger and social worker from Russia. She has been coming and going to Varanasi for the past 10 years. Here she stays in a guest house located in the lane leading to Narad Ghat. Natasha has large tattoos on both her hands and neck. She applies ash and sandalwood tilak on her forehead. Natasha enjoys spending time in the company of sadhus and saints. She also serves helpless dogs living in the streets. She works on getting them treated, feeding them, and protecting them from the cold. She also keeps sharing videos through Instagram about her life in India, spiritual experiences and especially caring for stray dogs. Her profile particularly shows content related to treating injured animals, feeding street dogs and raising voice against animal cruelty. Know what the people living in the lane say Yash Chaturvedi, who lives in the neighborhood where Natasha stays, said - She comes here every year. She has a lot of affection for the dogs living here. Natasha takes care of stray dogs and treats them herself. If someone beats or mistreats these dogs in front of her, she becomes furious with anger. Natasha says that the sense of belonging and compassion she found in the lanes of Kashi inspired her to serve the helpless dogs here. Natasha has taken a pledge that as long as possible, she will come to Kashi every year and continue to help these voiceless creatures. Dressed 100 street dogs in clothes during winter This year during the winter season, Natasha had specially prepared clothes for more than 100 stray dogs roaming the streets of Varanasi. Natasha herself went around the streets and dressed them in clothes. So that they could get relief from the cold. The street dogs are so attached to Natasha that even after months, when they see her, they hug her. They start kissing Natasha with joy.

stories.title: Police raid at Mukhtar Ansari's house at midnight:Son and Mau MLA Abbas questioned over stay; notice served
stories.summary: Police raided the ancestral residence of mafia Mukhtar Ansari in Ghazipur late Sunday night. Police had received information that Mukhtar's son and Mau MLA Abbas Ansari were staying there unauthorizedly. When the police arrived, the gate did not open for about 15 minutes. However, when the gate opened, and a team of 20 police personnel led by CO Sudhakar Pandey entered inside, Abbas Ansari was found inside. CO asked- Permission was granted by the Supreme Court to stay at the ancestral residence for only three days from May 13, whose period has already expired. After this, if any written permission has been received from the Supreme Court or High Court, it should be shown. CO also questioned Abbas about changing the gunner. To this, Abbas Ansari said that the case in which the Supreme Court had imposed a ban has been closed in the High Court. He also said that he was only prohibited from staying in his electoral constituency, Mau. He had already given written information to the Mau DM and SP about staying in Ghazipur. Abbas Ansari also showed some documents to the police. After this, the police handed him a notice, in which information about the order regarding his stay in Ghazipur was sought within 24 hours. After this, the police left. Meanwhile, Mau SP Kamlesh Bahadur says that no such permission has been given by the Mau police. See the pictures of the raid Now read what conversation took place between the CO and Abbas Ansari CO Sudhakar Pandey- You had permission from the Supreme Court to stay here for only 3 days. The period expired on May 15. Now, under which written order are you staying here? If there is any written order from the Supreme Court or High Court, please show it. Abbas Ansari- The Supreme Court had only imposed a ban on staying in Mau. There was no ban on Mohammadabad. I keep coming and going here. I had also come a few days ago for my maternal uncle's demise (death). Anyway, the case for which there was a ban from the Supreme Court, that case itself has been dismissed by the High Court. Still, regarding staying in Ghazipur, I had given written information to the DM and SP of Mau. If you had checked with them once, you wouldn't have had to face this trouble. (Abbas showed written documents.) CO- The order copy that we received had permission for only 3 days from May 13. After that, we don't have any order copy. If you have it, please show it to us. Abbas Ansari- I told you that the case has been closed. When the case was closed, I went to meet the Mau DM-SP. I have come after giving them written information. Abbas Ansari- I have also got a new gunner. If there was any such matter, how would I get a gunner from Mau? CO- That will be available, but why was the gunner changed? Why was the old one removed? Abbas Ansari- The old gunner had taken too much leave. He had asked me for one day's leave, saying his wife's delivery, but didn't return for 9 days. When the officers came to know about this, they themselves removed him. Abbas Ansari- You came here for such a small matter; you could have just called once. This matter could have been done over the phone. (After this, the CO handed over the notice to Abbas Ansari. Got signatures on the receiving. The police left around 11:35 at night.) SC imposed stay in the Chitrakoot gangster case Mohammadabad CO Sudhakar Pandey said- Abbas Ansari was allowed to stay at his ancestral residence in Yusufpur, Mohammadabad, Ghazipur for 3 days. This period ended on May 15. Information was received that he continued to stay there even after that. He comes and sleeps at night. We went to investigate this on the instructions of senior officials. Mau SP Kamlesh Bahadur said- No permission was given by Mau Police. Only the Supreme Court's order is valid. We have not received any new order from the court so far.

stories.title: CM Yogi attends Prateek Yadav's 'terawi' ceremony:Entire Yadav family, including Akhilesh and Dimple, attends the ceremony
stories.summary: The ‘tehravi’ ceremony of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav’s brother Prateek Yadav was held on Monday. During the programme, Prateek’s wife, Aparna Yadav, distributed pooris among attendees. When people raised slogans of “Prateek Bhaiya Amar Rahein,” she became emotional and broke down in tears. Folding her hands in greeting, she later went inside the house. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also attended the ceremony and paid tribute to Prateek while consoling Aparna. Akhilesh Yadav, Shivpal Yadav, Dimple Yadav and other family members reached Aparna’s residence. Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi also distributed pooris. Folk singer Malini Awasthi and actor Rajpal Yadav were among those present. The ritual was held at Aparna Yadav’s residence on Vikramaditya Marg in Lucknow, where devotional Ramdhun chants were played. Hoardings carrying condolence messages related to Prateek’s tehravi were also put up across several parts of the city. Prateek Yadav died of a heart attack on the morning of May 13 at the age of 38. His last rites were performed the next day at Baikunth Dham crematorium in Lucknow, with his father-in-law, Arvind Singh Bisht, lighting the pyre. On May 16, his ashes were immersed at the VVIP Ghat in Haridwar. Aparna travelled to Uttarakhand with her daughters on a chartered flight, accompanied by Shivpal Yadav’s son Aditya Yadav. stories.title: Child dies falling from zip line after safety belt opens:Father says, 'I brought him for a trip, how do I take his body home?'
stories.summary: A 15-year-old son of a bangle businessman died after falling from a 45-foot-high zip line in Agra. A video of the incident has also surfaced. The footage shows that as the teenager moved towards the other end of the zip line, the hook attached to his safety belt came loose, causing him to fall. The boy died in front of his parents after suffering critical injuries. The incident took place on Sunday in the Tajganj area of the city. Kunal Agarwal had come to Agra from Firozabad with his parents for a visit. Following the accident, police suspended the operation of the zip line and took the operator into custody. The family has alleged negligence by the zip line staff. See 2 pictures- Parents sat beside son’s body and wept Pankaj Agarwal, a bangle trader from Firozabad, had arrived in Agra with his family on Sunday. After visiting the Taj Mahal in the morning, the family went to Tajganj Chaupati. According to the family, Kunal became excited after seeing the zip line and insisted on trying it. His father eventually agreed. Eyewitnesses said staff members helped the teenager onto the zip line, secured the belt and released him towards the other end. During the ride, the boy reportedly first struck a metal net before falling directly to the ground. His parents rushed to him immediately, but he had already died. After the accident, the grieving parents sat beside their son’s body and broke down in tears. Police later arrived at the scene, consoled the family and sent the body for post-mortem examination. Father alleges lack of medical assistance Kunal’s father said his son died due to the negligence of the zip line operators. Crying after the incident, he said: “I brought my son here for a trip. Now how do I take his body back home?” He alleged there was no first-aid facility at the venue and no vehicle available to take the boy to hospital immediately. According to him, the delay in treatment cost his son his life. He said timely medical care might have saved the teenager. Police Commissioner orders strict action Agra Police Commissioner Deepak Kumar visited the accident site and inspected the area. He directed officials to conduct an impartial investigation and take strict action against those found responsible. ADCP Himanshu Gaurav said adherence to safety standards is crucial in adventure activities. He added that the initial investigation had raised serious concerns regarding safety equipment and arrangements. Police are now trying to determine whether the accident occurred due to technical failure or negligence. Adventure activities began after private contract The Agra Development Authority developed the Chaupati area in Tajganj in 2023 on the lines of Jaipur’s Masala Chowk. Initially, the site attracted both tourists and local residents, but visitor numbers later declined. In October last year, the operation contract was handed over to EOD Adventure Private Limited. The company introduced activities including zip-lining, zip-cycling, go-karting and bull riding, after which the venue again started attracting adventure enthusiasts. What is a Zip Line? A zip line is an adventure activity similar to a suspended aerial ride. In this activity, a strong cable or wire is stretched between two elevated points. Participants are attached to the cable using a safety belt and hook, allowing them to slide rapidly from one end to the other while suspended in the air. Because of the speed and height involved, zip-lining is considered a high-adrenaline adventure sport.

stories.title: US Secretary of State visits Taj Mahal with wife:Poses for photos sitting on the Diana Bench, asks guide about the monument
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited the Taj Mahal with his wife Jeanette Rubio on Monday morning. The couple reached the monument at around 10:15 am. Marco Rubio was seen wearing a black coat and trousers, while Jeanette Rubio wore a grey gown. Amid the scorching 41°C heat, both wore dark sunglasses as they admired the Taj Mahal. During the visit, Rubio asked guide Nitin Singh, several questions related to the monument and its history. Couple poses on Diana Bench After touring the monument, Marco and Jeanette Rubio posed for photographs while sitting on the iconic Diana Bench. During the photo session, Rubio was seen with his arm around Jeanette’s waist. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor later joined them on the bench, and the three posed together for photographs. Jeanette Rubio described the Taj Mahal as “extremely beautiful”. 60-member delegation also accompanied Rubio A delegation of around 60 people accompanying Rubio also arrived in Agra. After spending around 45 minutes inside the Taj Mahal complex, the delegation left for Hotel Amar Vilas. Rubio is scheduled to have lunch there before departing for Jaipur by special flight at 12:50 pm. Received at Airport by Commissioner and DM Earlier, Rubio was received at Kheria Airport by Commissioner Deepak Kumar and District Magistrate Manish Bansal. From the airport, he travelled directly to the Taj Mahal and used a golf cart to reach the main complex. Ahead of the visit, barricading had been put in place at the Taj Mahal premises and tourists inside the monument complex were asked to leave. See photos- Significance of visit amid India-US tensions Rubio has been on a four-day visit to India since Saturday, 23rd May. During the visit, he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Seva Teerth and conveyed an invitation from former US President Donald Trump for Modi to visit the United States. Rubio’s visit comes at a time when India-US relations have witnessed tensions over several issues since the middle of last year. Diplomatic observers believe the trip is aimed at strengthening ties between the two countries once again.

stories.title: 'Main rahun na rahun, humesha saath rahunga':Premanand Ji appeal devotees to focus on Shri Ji; 'padyatra' stopped for 9 days after his health deteriorated
stories.summary: Premanand Maharaj has issued an emotional appeal to his disciples and devotees through a video message released from Vrindavan. The 1-minute-19-second video was uploaded on Sunday on the official YouTube channel of Kelly Kunj Ashram Trust. In the message, Premanand Maharaj said- Do not worry at all. Whether we meet or not, whether we speak or not, we love all of you very much. The most important thing is that you should not worry. Do not think about how we will continue. We will remain in your minds even without speaking. Night Padyatra stopped for 9 days Premanand Maharaj’s nightly padyatra has remained suspended since May 17, raising concerns among devotees about his health. His disciples had earlier informed followers that his health condition was not stable. Private meetings and personal interactions with devotees have also been stopped. According to those close to him, both of Premanand Maharaj’s kidneys are damaged, and he undergoes dialysis two to three times every week. In the latest message, he reassured followers and urged them to continue devotional practices. He said- You should follow what Gurudev says. Remain completely carefree. Whatever service you are engaged in, continue doing it. Chant God’s name constantly. It will be auspicious. Your Gurudev will remain in your mind. Perform bhajans fearlessly, without worry or sorrow. Whenever we feel like it, we will speak again. Premanand Maharaj also spoke about his decision to remain in solitude. He said- We are observing solitude. This solitude is for you, not for us. We are not doing bhajans for ourselves. Our silence is not for us. To tell you the truth, whatever was destined for us has already happened. Whatever is happening now is happening for you. Perform bhajans, chant God’s name, remain dependent on Him, stay happy and stay joyful. Thousands returned disappointed on May 17 Premanand Maharaj’s nightly foot pilgrimage has remained suspended for the past nine days. Private darshan and conversations have also stopped during this period. On the night of May 17, thousands of devotees had gathered for his darshan, expecting him to begin his routine 3 am walk. However, instead of Premanand Maharaj, his disciples arrived and announced over loudspeakers. They told devotees- Due to Maharaj Ji’s ill health, the nightly padyatra is being cancelled from today. We request everyone not to gather along the roadside. After the announcement, many devotees returned disappointed without receiving darshan. Visited Varah Ghat two days ago Despite his health concerns, Premanand Maharaj visited Guru Saint Govind Sharan Maharaj’s ashram at Varah Ghat two days ago. He travelled there from Kelly Kunj Ashram to meet the saint. Premanand Maharaj waks 1.5 kilometres daily Normally, Premanand Maharaj leaves Kelly Kunj Ashram at around 3 am and walks nearly 1.5 kilometres to Saubhari Van. Thousands of devotees gather daily to catch a glimpse of him during the walk. On ordinary days, around 20,000 devotees reportedly attend. During weekends and major festivals, the number rises sharply and can reach several lakh. Left home at the age of 13 Premanand Maharaj was born in Akhri village in Narwal tehsil of Kanpur district. His father is Shambhu Narayan Pandey and his mother is Rama Devi. He has three brothers and is the middle sibling. During childhood, he was known as Anirudh Kumar Pandey and was spiritually inclined from an early age. He studied up to Class 8. As a child, he wanted to build a platform for a Shiva temple along with his friends. Construction work had begun, but some local people reportedly stopped it. The incident deeply upset him and eventually led him to leave home. He travelled to Kashi via Kanpur. At the age of 13, he decided to become a Brahmachari. Initially, he was given the name ‘Aryan Brahmachari’. He spent around 15 months in Kashi and later received initiation from Guru Gauri Sharan Ji Maharaj before eventually arriving in Mathura. From Sanyasi to Radhavallabhi Saint After reaching Vrindavan, Premanand Maharaj regularly visited Banke Bihari Temple. He gradually developed a deep interest in Rasleela and began attending programmes associated with the Radhavallabh tradition. According to his followers, he would stand for hours listening to spiritual discourses. One day, a saint recited a verse from Shri Radharassudhanidhi, but Premanand Maharaj could not understand its meaning. Later, during a circumambulation of Vrindavan, he heard a sakhi singing the same verse. The words affected him deeply. He approached the sakhi and asked for the meaning of the shloka. The sakhi reportedly replied- To understand its meaning, it is necessary to become a Radhavallabhi. It was after this incident that Premanand Maharaj embraced the Radhavallabhi tradition.

stories.title: Shankaracharya to buy cows through ‘Go-LX' app:Says licences will be issued to caretakers; 4,000 Gau-Dhams to be set up across India
stories.summary: Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati is set to launch the Go-LX app as part of his cow protection campaign. Speaking during his ongoing cow protection yatra, the Shankaracharya said the platform would only facilitate the ‘purchase’ of cows, not their sale. He said anyone from the Sanatani community wishing to take responsibility for a cow would have to sign an agreement. A licence would also be issued stating that the cow was being taken for service and protection purposes. He added that periodic checks would be conducted to ensure the animals remain safe and properly cared for. According to the Shankaracharya, ‘Gau-Dham’ centres will be opened in all 4,123 Assembly constituencies across the country to house cows purchased through the platform. He clarified that the initiative is meant only for indigenous Indian cows and not for foreign breeds. Three main features of the Go-LX app Only ‘Purchase’, No sale Although the process on the app will function in a manner similar to OLX, the platform will only facilitate the “purchase” of cows. Organisations and Sanatani individuals will be able to take indigenous Indian breed cows directly from farmers under their protection by offering “neg-nyochhawar” — a traditional offering or donation. Crowd funding for cow care The organisation said it does not currently have sufficient funds for fodder and maintenance of cows. Under the proposed system, multiple people will be able to collectively take responsibility for one cow. Licence and service agreement If someone wishes to take a cow from Gau-Dham to their home for service, Jyotishpeeth will issue a “Cow Rearing Licence” along with a formal agreement. If the individual later becomes unable to care for the cow, it must be returned to the Gau-Dham. Now read the conversation with Shankaracharya When will the Go-LX website and app be launched? Our app and website, 1008.guru, are already available. We are now adding this feature to the same platform. The technicians associated with us say it will take around 20 to 25 days to develop the new app feature. We will launch it once it is ready.” Why did you choose the name Go-LX? We did not choose the name because OLX is widely advertised. The name was selected because people are familiar with the OLX process. If we communicate in a language the younger generation understands, they will grasp the message quickly. How will ordinary people list cows on the platform? This is a different kind of process. There is no buying and selling here; there is only purchasing. People wanting to give away cows will post s on the app. We will take responsibility for cows from any part of the country. Our intention is not to sell cows. We will care for them throughout their lives. Where will all these cows be kept? We are discussing this. Naturally, cows from across the country cannot be transported to one place. At least one unit will need to be established in every state so that cows remain within their respective states. Where will funding for the campaign come from? Three kinds of funding are required, first, to acquire cows; second, to build shelters; and third, for fodder, water and medicines. We are not wealthy industrialists. We do not have money, but we do have determination. Sanatani people are contacting us. We tell them that they should buy at least one cow themselves so that it is saved from slaughter. If they face difficulty caring for the cow, they can keep it at our Gau-Dham. The cow will still belong to them. Through the website, we will provide daily updates about the animal’s condition. They can take the cow back whenever they wish. How will Gau-Dham centres be managed? Ideally, one Gau-Dham will be established in each of the country’s 4,123 Assembly constituencies. The area of one Assembly constituency is not so large that it cannot be managed properly. In this way, owners will be able to visit Gau-Dham, feed the cows, care for them and serve them personally. There will be a central management team. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) will be created and every Gau-Dham will function according to those SOPs. Will only your organisation be able to acquire cows through the app? We have already said that anyone can take responsibility for a cow. Our aim is not to gather cows in one place. Our objective is to save them from slaughter. At present, the media is portraying a narrative that Hindus earn their livelihood only by selling cows. This initiative is against that narrative. What qualifications will cow caretakers need? Anyone taking a cow through us will receive a licence from Jyotishpeeth stating that they have signed a bond for the cow’s service. The person will sign an agreement stating that the cow is being taken for service purposes. If they are later unable to care for it, they will not sell it elsewhere but return it to us. Will the app deal only with old cows? It is not true that only old cows are sent for slaughter. Since our aim is to prevent slaughter, cows of every category will be included. We will develop a system to ensure proper maintenance, healthcare and breeding of registered cows. Periodic inspections will also be conducted. Will funds also be raised through the app? Certainly, funding will be required. But this will not be a system where people simply hand over money to us. When a cow becomes available, it will be displayed on the platform along with the required amount. People will be informed that if the cow is not taken, it may go for slaughter. Several people can collectively take responsibility for one cow. They may either keep the cow themselves or allow it to remain in our Gaushala. How will cow prices be decided? The owner of any property has the right to decide its value. We are not truly ‘buyers’ of cows. We only use the word because it is commonly understood. In reality, no one should have the right either to buy or sell cows. The idea is simply that the cow will remain with us, and in return, the owner may accept an offering or donation.

stories.title: Brother and sister carried nurse’s body on scooter in Meerut:Siblings allegedly strangled her to death on 21 May; 2 CCTV clips surface
stories.summary: Two CCTV footages linked to the murder of 25-year-old staff nurse Anjali Sharma in Meerut have surfaced. Both videos were collected by Anjali’s family members themselves during their own investigation into the case. In the first footage, the main accused, Sufiyan and his sister Sajida are seen carrying Anjali’s body on a scooter. Her feet can be seen dragging along the road before a young man from the neighbourhood runs forward and places them properly on the vehicle. The second footage shows a woman wearing what appears to be a nurse’s apron arriving at Sufiyan’s rented room shortly after the body was removed. Police are now trying to identify the woman and determine why she visited the house after the alleged murder. Both videos were captured by a CCTV camera installed in a house located in the lane opposite Sufiyan’s residence. Police have arrested both main accused, Sufiyan and his sister Sajida. The murder reportedly took place on the afternoon of May 21. First CCTV footage: Body carried on scooter In the first CCTV clip, Sajida is seen wearing lowers, a T-shirt and a dupatta. She had covered her face with a helmet and was seated at the front of the scooter. Sufiyan is then seen bringing Anjali’s body out of his rented room. The two struggle to balance the scooter while placing their bodies between them. The body repeatedly tilts from side to side as they attempt to steady it. Sajida drives the scooter while Sufiyan sits behind, holding the body upright in the middle. As they begin moving, Anjali’s feet drag on the road. Seeing this, a local youth rushes towards them and lifts her legs back onto the scooter. Residents of the area gathered after witnessing the disturbing scene. However, the accused allegedly attempted to mislead them. Sufiyan told neighbours she had fallen ill When neighbours questioned Sufiyan and Sajida about what had happened, Sufiyan reportedly claimed that Anjali had suddenly fallen ill. He allegedly told residents that she had suffered heatstroke, was unconscious and unable to speak or walk, and that they were taking her to a doctor. Despite his explanation, locals reportedly remained suspicious. However, assuming it to be a personal matter involving tenants, nobody intervened further. Later, when news of the murder surfaced through the media, residents realised that the duo had been transporting Anjali’s body. Police said the accused later abandoned the body outside Lala Lajpat Rai Medical College. Second CCTV footage raises new questions A short while after Sufiyan and Sajida left with the body, another woman was captured on CCTV entering the rented house. The woman appeared to be wearing a coat resembling a nurse’s apron, leading investigators to suspect she may be connected to the medical profession. The footage shows the woman arriving at the house and speaking to a man believed to be Sufiyan. Both are seen talking while moving around outside the house before the woman leaves. Police are now trying to identify who the woman is, where she came from, and what connection she may have to the case. Investigators are examining whether she had prior knowledge of the incident. Family found key evidence themselves Anjali Sharma’s elder brother Pradeep Sharma and elder sister, Neha Sharma, claimed they discovered the CCTV footage themselves after visiting the crime scene. According to the family, when they reached Sufiyan’s rented accommodation, they found the house open and unsealed, despite it being the alleged crime scene. The siblings then spoke to neighbours and checked CCTV cameras installed in the locality. The crucial footage was eventually recovered from a building opposite the rented house. The family has questioned why police failed to immediately secure the premises. Anjali’s marriage dispute and relationship with Sufiyan Anjali, a resident of Jagriti Vihar Sector-3, worked as a staff nurse at Lala Lajpat Rai Medical College. She married Sunny, a resident of Medical Sector-8, in 2018. The couple have a five-year-old son. According to family members, the couple had been facing marital disputes for nearly a year and divorce proceedings are currently underway in court. Anjali had reportedly been living with her brother Pradeep for the past year. During her work at the medical college, she came into contact with Sufiyan, a resident of Lisari Gate, who worked there as a ward boy. The two later developed a relationship. Family members alleged that Sufiyan had been pressuring Anjali to convert her religion and marry him, but she refused. Alleged argument over marriage led to murder According to police, accused Sajida told investigators that Anjali had come to Lohianagar on May 21. An argument allegedly broke out between Sufiyan and Anjali over marriage. Sajida claimed she also joined the argument. Police said both siblings then allegedly strangled Anjali to death. According to the confession, they initially transported the body on a scooter and later shifted it onto an e-rickshaw before abandoning it outside the medical college. Hospital authorities later informed police and Anjali’s brother about the body. Following the information, SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle reached the spot. CCTV footage from the hospital area allegedly showed Sajida travelling in an e-rickshaw. Police detained Sajida and her mother within 1.5 hours of the incident. Sufiyan was arrested on Sunday night. Sister alleges religious conversion pressure and financial fraud Anjali’s sister Neha, alleged that Sufiyan had been blackmailing her sister and pressuring her to convert and marry him. She claimed to have seen messages on Anjali’s mobile phone in which Sufiyan allegedly asked her to leave her husband and child, convert her religion and marry him. According to Neha, when Anjali refused, he murdered her. Neha further said she had directly asked Anjali whether she intended to marry Sufiyan, but Anjali replied that they were “just friends”. She last met her sister on May 19, when Anjali visited her house because her mother-in-law was injured. Neha said that after receiving news of the murder on May 21, she rushed to the spot and saw marks around Anjali’s neck, along with signs of dragging and assault on her hands and feet. The family also alleged that Sufiyan had cheated Anjali out of ₹5 lakh by promising her a permanent appointment. Police sealed house two days later The rented house in Lohianagar, where Anjali allegedly died was sealed only on the evening of May 23, was two days after the incident. According to the family, Sajida and Sufiyan had already confessed during questioning that the body had been brought from the same house. Despite this, police allegedly failed to secure the crime scene immediately. When Anjali’s family visited the house on May 23, they found it open and informed the police. Only afterwards was the property sealed. Family members have alleged that evidence may have been tampered with during the two-day delay.

stories.title: Storm, rain and lightning alert in 14 UP districts:Heatwave warning issued in 53; Banda country’s second-hottest city at 46.8°C
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh remains in the grip of intense heat and heatwave conditions. Bright sunshine was visible across the state from Monday morning, while slow wind speeds increased humidity levels and discomfort. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for thunderstorms, rainfall and lightning in 14 districts of Purvanchal today. At the same time, 53 districts are under heatwave alert, including 10 districts placed under red alert. A red alert means scorching sunshine and extremely hot winds are expected in these areas. Nautapa begins today, heat expected to intensify further Nautapa has also begun from today, marking the start of a nine-day period traditionally associated with extreme heat. Weather officials say conditions are likely to worsen during this period, with temperatures in most districts expected to remain above 45°C. Banda becomes country’s second-hottest city More than 50 cities in the state remained under heatwave conditions on Sunday. Banda emerged as the country’s second-hottest city, recording a maximum temperature of 46.8°C. Brahmapuri in Maharashtra’s Vidarbha region was the hottest city in the country at 47.2°C. Other major temperatures recorded in UP included- Green shades installed at traffic signals in Lucknow In Lucknow, green shade covers were installed at traffic signals to provide relief to commuters from the harsh sunlight. Meanwhile, in Moradabad, a Provincial Guard (PRD) personnel managing traffic reportedly died, with heatstroke suspected to be the cause. In Muzaffarnagar, a moving car caught fire. A woman, children and the driver jumped out of the vehicle to save themselves. See weather pictures- Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said temperatures in UP have remained extremely high over the past few days. According to him, intense heating has created a large difference between ground temperatures and upper atmospheric temperatures, resulting in conditions favourable for storms and rainfall. He added that a trough line extending from Eastern UP towards Chhattisgarh is also active, increasing the chances of strong winds, lightning and light rainfall. However, he clarified that there is little possibility of a significant drop in temperatures and the state will continue to remain under the grip of heatwave conditions. Weather forecast for the next five days May 26- Bright sunshine is expected across the state, along with heatwave conditions. Dust storms may occur in Eastern UP. May 27- Severe heat will continue across UP, with most districts likely to remain under heatwave conditions. Rain is possible in Eastern UP. May 28- Some areas of Eastern UP may receive rainfall. Isolated showers are also possible in parts of Western UP. May 29- Light rainfall is likely across the state. Temperatures may decline slightly, although humidity levels will remain high. May 30- Weather fluctuations will continue. Drizzle and strong winds are expected, but there will be no major relief from the heat.

stories.title: How big is power crisis in UP?:Why ‘unscheduled power cuts’ become inevitable in summer
stories.summary: On one hand, temperatures in Uttar Pradesh are touching new highs every day. On the other, power cuts from cities to villages have triggered widespread public anger. The Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) has set a record by supplying more than 30,000 megawatts of electricity. However, it is still unable to meet public demand. With the Assembly elections due next year, even BJP legislators appear worried. Several BJP MLAs have written directly to Energy Minister A. K. Sharma over the worsening electricity situation. On May 23, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath suspended two engineers of the Transmission Corporation, Ghaziabad Executive Engineer Rahul Kumar and Meerut Executive Engineer Yogesh Kumar. Two other engineers were issued adverse entries and warnings. Why do power cuts intensify in UP every May and June? Is it poor management or systemic helplessness? Here is a detailed look. Huge gap between electricity demand and supply Over the past three years, electricity demand in the state during May has risen by 4,000 to 5,000 MW. This can be understood from figures released by Energy Minister AK Sharma. On May 20, 2024, peak electricity demand stood at 26,433 MW. On May 20, 2025, demand rose to 29,138 MW. This year, demand touched 30,458 MW on May 20. This means demand has increased by nearly 4,000 MW compared to 2024. However, supply continues to fall short by around 850 MW to 1,000 MW daily. This gap is resulting in scheduled and unscheduled power cuts across both urban and rural areas. Another major issue is the gap between transmission capacity and consumer load. UP currently has 3.73 crore electricity consumers. The sanctioned load of these connections is 8.57 crore kilowatts, while the capacity of the Corporation’s 132 KV substations is only 6.25 crore kilowatts, a difference of nearly 2 crore kilowatts. With extreme heat forcing households to fully utilise their sanctioned load, the system is struggling to supply uninterrupted electricity to all consumers simultaneously. Why are power cuts worse at night? One question troubling consumers is why power cuts become more frequent during the night. During daytime hours, solar energy supplements electricity supply, reducing shortages. However, at night, supply depends mainly on hydro, thermal (coal-based) and nuclear power generation. As a result, even though electricity demand in UP peaks between 2 pm and 3:30 pm, the department somehow manages to meet it during the day. The real crisis begins at night. The peak consumption period in the state is between 8 pm and midnight. Electricity usage is highest during these four hours, but availability is comparatively lower. This imbalance between demand and supply makes load shedding unavoidable. Public anger rising over lack of response In the middle of intense summer heat, residents are unable to sleep peacefully because of prolonged power cuts. When consumers call substations to register complaints, they are often redirected to helpline number 1912. However, callers say they rarely receive satisfactory responses. Officials sometimes cite software updates and at other times blame technical faults for outages. Frustrated residents have increasingly resorted to protests, gheraos of substations and demonstrations on the streets. Transformers burning out, cables catching fire The Central government had sanctioned nearly ₹44,000 crore under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) to strengthen UP’s electricity infrastructure. The funds were meant for replacing old and damaged cables, increasing transformer capacity and constructing new 33/11 KV and 132 KV substations. Government data shows work has been carried out over the past decade. However, the improvements are proving inadequate compared to the state’s growing demand. Many areas still operate with low-capacity transformers, which frequently fail or catch fire when the load increases. UPPCL data shows that, on average, more than 44 transformers are burning out every day in the state. While damaged transformers are generally replaced within the stipulated time in cities, villages often have to wait a week or even a month for replacement. Until then, residents are left without electricity. Armoured cables have also been installed in both rural and urban areas. These include aluminium and copper cables of varying capacities. However, most of the state’s armoured network is aluminium-based. These cables range from 4 sq mm to 50 sq mm in thickness and can handle electrical flow between 15 kW and 55 kW. When the load exceeds their capacity, the cables burn out. With electricity demand soaring during the heatwave, even these cables are unable to bear the pressure. Vertical system failing at substations More than 15,000 contractual workers have reportedly been removed from service in UP. A large number of Assistant Engineers (AEs) have also been suspended or attached to offices. This has created a serious manpower crisis at a time when the power system faces its toughest months, May to July. During this period, electricity demand reaches its peak, storms and strong winds trigger faults, and technical breakdowns rise sharply. However, there are not enough linemen available to repair faults quickly. The electricity department currently operates a “three-gang” system at substations. Each gang includes one lineman and two helpers, working in 8-hour shifts. A single substation covers around 3–4 km in urban areas, and 12–15 km in rural regions. If multiple faults occur simultaneously, teams take several hours to attend to all complaints. In many cases, consumers have to endure outages for three to four hours before repairs begin. Who is responsible for power cuts in UP? (In this survey by LocalCircles, people were given 7 options. People chose more than one option.) What Needs to Be Done? Awadhesh Verma, President of the Consumer Council, suggested several measures to improve UP’s electricity system. Reinstatement of Contract Workers Dismissed contractual workers should be brought back to strengthen fault-repair capacity. Return of Suspended Engineers Assistant Engineers suspended for long periods should be reinstated and assigned field duties. Addressing the Manpower Crisis Additional technical staff should be recruited across all power companies to tackle severe shortages. Strengthening the Response System The number of technical teams and repair gangs should be increased to ensure quicker restoration during breakdowns. Reforming the Vertical System The current grievance redressal mechanism should be made faster and more transparent so complaints are not left unresolved. Fixing Management Accountability Despite investment of nearly ₹44,094 crore, accountability for poor performance and infrastructure failure must be fixed. BJP MLAs worried over public anger The electricity crisis has now become politically sensitive. With continuous power cuts amid severe heat, protests are erupting across the state. Opposition parties including the Samajwadi Party, Bahujan Samaj Party and Indian National Congress, have intensified their attacks on the government. At the same time, BJP legislators also appear concerned about the political fallout ahead of next year’s Assembly elections. BJP MLAs Rajeshwar Singh and Dr Neeraj Bora, along with Minister Manoj Pandey, have written to the Energy Minister demanding immediate improvements in the electricity system. Meanwhile, BJP MLA Ashok Kumar from Salon alleged that officials do not listen even to elected representatives. He accused them of extorting money during checking drives and disconnecting electricity without prior notice. BSP chief Mayawati also criticised the government on social media, saying it is the administration’s responsibility to provide relief to people during extreme heat. Akhilesh Yadav vs AK Sharma on Social Media A sharp political exchange has also broken out online between SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and Energy Minister AK Sharma. Akhilesh Yadav’s allegation Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP government of creating the crisis through poor policies. He claimed the government neither established new power plants nor upgraded the transmission network. He also alleged corruption in the installation of smart meters. He appealed to the public not to vent their anger on junior employees and linemen. Energy Minister’s response AK Sharma countered that the electricity system in UP has improved significantly compared to the Samajwadi Party government between 2012 and 2017. stories.title: Hamirpur bridge collapse caused by negligence, not storm:Deputy project manager absent from site for 3 days
stories.summary: The bridge being built over the Betwa River in Hamirpur claimed the lives of six workers. After the accident, the State Bridge Corporation said the slab collapsed due to strong winds and a storm. However, the reality is that the tragedy was caused by negligence on the part of the construction company and Bridge Corporation officials. The Deputy Project Manager of the Bridge Corporation had not visited the site for the past three days. He left the work entirely in the hands of the contractor hired by the construction company. To cut costs, the contractor reportedly used weak support structures, which collapsed when the storm hit. Following the Chief Minister’s strict response, the Managing Director of the State Bridge Corporation, Dharmveer Singh, suspended the Assistant Engineer (AE). A departmental inquiry has also been ordered against the Deputy Project Manager. Know the negligence behind the accident Negligence 1: Cable installed but not tightened, slab collapses during storm The technical reason behind the accident has raised serious questions. According to Vijay Pratap Singh, director of Kanpur-based company ‘The Shelter’, the bridge segment slab was cast below and later lifted onto the pillar. Although the cable was installed on Thursday, it was not tightened and was scheduled to be secured on Friday. Before that could happen, a storm struck at night. Despite a weather alert issued by the UP Relief Department for storms between May 28 and 31, the heavy structure was left on temporary and weak support without being locked, which experts termed a major negligence. Negligence 2: Entire work left to contractor, project manager absent for days Suspended Setu Nigam Assistant Engineer Gajendra Chaudhary allegedly left the entire slab installation process to the contractor’s inexperienced engineers and labourers instead of supervising it himself. At the same time, Deputy Project Manager Dilip Kumar had reportedly not visited the site for the past two to three days. He also failed to inspect the tender conditions and the quality of materials being used. Negligence 3: No shelter for workers during storm Kanpur-based company ‘The Shelter’, located in Naubasta (Baba Nagar), was allegedly carrying out work while ignoring basic safety norms. No proper shed or accommodation had been arranged for labourers staying at the site. Due to the lack of shelter, workers were forced to run for safety when the storm hit, worsening the situation during the accident. Officer under scanner included in probe committee After the bridge collapse, Setu Nigam formed a three-member high-level departmental inquiry committee comprising the Joint Managing Director, Chief Project Manager (Design), and Kanpur Chief Project Manager (CPM) V.K. Sen. However, questions have been raised within the department as the entire project was being supervised by CPM V.K. Sen himself. Critics questioned how an officer linked to the project could be part of the investigation committee. Clarifying the decision, Corporation MD Dharamveer Singh said V.K. Sen was included only to present technical records and facts before the committee and would not participate in decision-making. Contractor has political connections Vijay Pratap Singh, director of ‘The Shelter’ company, is the brother of Pawan Pratap Singh, the BJP’s regional minister for the Kanpur region. He is also said to have close links with BJP state vice-president Manvendra Singh Chauhan, Legislative Council Chairman Kunwar Manvendra Singh, and several MLAs from Kanpur. Government's action Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, showing strictness immediately after the accident, instructed Setu Nigam, MD Dharamveer Singh, to reach the spot. He directed to give a compensation of Rs 5 lakh each to the families of the deceased and Rs 50,000 each to the injured. He said, The matter will be investigated. Strict action will be taken against the culprits.

stories.title: Engineer dies after falling from 190-foot tower:Had climbed to check signal in Greater Noida, safety belt lock breaks
stories.summary: A 30-year-old engineer died after falling from a mobile tower in Greater Noida while checking a network malfunction. The incident took place on Thursday evening in Chandpur village under the Rabupura area. According to reports, the engineer had climbed the tower to inspect a signal issue when the lock of his safety belt reportedly broke. He then fell from a height of nearly 190 feet, leading to his death. The tower is said to belong to Airtel. The deceased was identified as Shantanu (30), a resident of Dharmpur village in Firozabad. Police reached the spot after the incident and began an investigation into the matter. See 2 pictures of the accident site Safety belt opened during signal check For the past several days, villagers in Chandpur had been facing network issues on an airtel tower installed in the area and had lodged complaints with the company. Following the complaint, network engineer Shantanu arrived at the site with his team on Friday to inspect the problem. Shantanu climbed the tower wearing a helmet and safety belt to check the signal at a height of nearly 190 feet. During the inspection, the lock of his safety belt suddenly broke, causing him to fall from the tower. Panic broke out at the spot after the accident. His colleagues, along with police personnel, rushed him to GIMS Hospital in Kasna, where doctors declared him dead. The incident triggered grief and chaos in his family after the news reached them. Police have sent the body for post-mortem and said the exact cause of the accident is being investigated. Brother said that he was working in Airtel for 4 years Shantanu's brother, Devesh Kumar, said, He used to work in the Airtel office located in Sector-62, Noida. He was a network engineer in the company for the last 4 years. Shantanu had come to the village on May 25 itself. He returned to Noida on May 27. He said that our mother's name is Meena Devi and father's name is Shyam. We are 4 siblings. Vijay Kumar and I are his elder brothers, while there is also a sister Chanchal. Shantanu was my youngest brother. Family members asked that why was he made to climb the tower after 5 PM? The deceased's elder sister-in-law, Kantesh, said, We received a call from Noida saying that your brother had fallen. After that, we called Shantanu, but his phone was not reachable. We also called a person who lived with Shantanu, but his phone was also switched off. Then our family members gathered and reached Noida, only then did we get information about the entire incident. This accident happened on Thursday evening between approximately 5:30 and 6 PM. Whereas, according to the rules, climbing the tower is not allowed after 5 PM. Despite this, he was made to climb the tower. Shantanu was on duty in the Bulandshahr-Meerut region. He was sent to the Noida site for work. Child also died in Agra due to safety belt breaking 5 days ago, an accident similar to Greater Noida also happened in Agra. On May 24, Kunal, the 16-year-old son of Firozabad bangle businessman Pankaj Agarwal and his wife, died after falling from a zip line swing in front of them. In Agra, he fell headfirst from a 45-foot high swing. As soon as Kunal moved from one end of the zip line to the other, the hook of his safety belt broke. He hit the railing and fell down. He died on the spot after struggling. When the son was on the zip line swing, his mother and younger brother were making a video of him below. The entire accident was recorded on their phone. Kunal's family had come to Agra from Firozabad for a visit.

stories.title: ₹1 lakh reward criminal killed in Saharanpur encounter:Rapid firing from both sides, inspector, constable shot during exchange of fire
stories.summary: A face-to-face encounter broke out between police and criminals in broad daylight in Uttar Pradesh’s Saharanpur on Thursday. During the exchange of fire, a criminal carrying a reward of ₹1 lakh was shot dead, while his accomplice managed to escape from the spot. According to police, the encounter took place near Doomwala village between the Sarsawa and Chilkana areas. The deceased criminal was hit by two bullets and died on the spot during the firing. During the operation, an inspector and a constable also sustained gunshot injuries after being hit by two bullets each. Both injured policemen were rushed to a hospital, where they are currently undergoing treatment. Police launched a search operation in the area to trace the absconding criminal. Further investigation into the case is underway. See 2 pictures Police received tip-off about criminal activity Police received information that two criminals were roaming between Pilkhani and Doomwala villages in the Sarsawa police station area with the intention of committing a crime. Acting on the tip-off, police launched a joint checking campaign in the area. During the operation on the Pilkhani-Doomwala road, the police team came face-to-face with the suspects. Seeing themselves surrounded, the criminals opened fire on the police team, prompting retaliatory firing by the police. Rewarded criminal shot dead, search on for absconding accused During the encounter, Ehsan, son of Riyasat and a resident of Kapoori village under Nakur police station area, was shot. According to police, he sustained bullet injuries to the chest and leg and died on the spot. Police said the deceased carried a reward of ₹1 lakh on his head. Meanwhile, one of his accomplices managed to escape from the spot by evading the police cordon. In the exchange of fire, Sarsawa police station in-charge Inspector Pravesh Sharma suffered two bullet injuries to his left hand. Head Constable Sonu was also injured by a bullet. Both injured policemen were admitted to a hospital for treatment, and their condition is reported to be stable. Following the incident, senior police officials reached the spot and reviewed the situation. An intensive search operation has been launched in nearby areas to arrest the absconding criminal. This news is being updated

stories.title: Rampur court overturns Abdullah Azam’s 7-year sentence:Relief in fake passport case, pending cases keep him jailed
stories.summary: Abdullah Azam, son of Samajwadi Party National General Secretary Azam Khan, who is lodged in Rampur jail, received major relief on Friday. The Rampur MP/MLA Sessions Court quashed the seven-year sentence awarded to him in the two-passport case. The Rampur court had sentenced Abdullah Azam to seven years in prison on December 5, 2025. A fine of Rs 50,000 was also imposed on him. Abdullah had challenged the verdict in the Sessions Court, where arguments were completed on May 25. While pronouncing the verdict on Friday, the court accepted Abdullah’s appeal and overturned the lower court’s order, acquitting him in the case. However, he will not be released from jail as several of his other cases are pending in the Supreme Court. Abdullah is currently lodged in Rampur jail along with his father Azam Khan in connection with their two PAN card case. Appeal was made to increase Akash Saxena's sentence Abdullah Azam’s lawyer Nasir Sultan said the case dates back to July 30, 2019, when BJP MLA Akash Saxena filed a complaint at the Civil Lines police station in Rampur. It was alleged that Abdullah had obtained two passports at different times using two separate date-of-birth certificates, which were later used as identity documents at various places. In the case, the trial court had sentenced Mohammad Abdullah Azam Khan to seven years in prison on December 5, 2025. Challenging that order, Abdullah approached the MP/MLA Sessions Court. The verdict was delivered on Friday, where the court accepted his appeal, overturned the lower court’s decision and acquitted him. The prosecution side, represented by BJP MLA Akash Saxena, had also filed an appeal seeking enhancement of Abdullah’s sentence, but the court rejected the plea. Azam and Abdullah kept making mistake after mistake Who is Mohammad Azam Khan? Azam Khan has been elected MLA from Rampur 10 times and has also served once as an MP. In 1980, to challenge the dominance of the Nawab family in Rampur, he formed unions of bidi workers, textile workers and rickshaw pullers, gradually building his own political identity in the district. Azam Khan has remained associated with controversies throughout his political career. He has faced allegations of making objectionable remarks against women, misbehaving with officials and using controversial language during elections. Has had a deep connection with controversies Azam Khan has remained associated with controversies throughout his political career. He has faced allegations of making objectionable remarks against women, misbehaving with officials and using controversial language during elections. During the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the Election Commission banned him from campaigning twice. Although he won the election, his membership was later revoked after he was sentenced to more than two years in a criminal case. A by-election was then held in Rampur, where BJP candidate Ghanshyam Lodhi emerged victorious. During the Samajwadi Party regime, Azam Khan was often referred to as the “Mini CM”. Now know about the complainant Akash Saxena... BJP MLA Akash Saxena, the complainant in the case, currently represents the Rampur city seat. After Azam Khan’s Assembly membership was revoked, by-elections were held on the Rampur Nagar seat on December 5, 2022, and the result was declared on December 7. In the bypoll, BJP candidate Akash Saxena defeated Azam Khan’s close aide Asim Raza by 25,703 votes. Earlier, Akash had also contested against Azam Khan in the 2022 Assembly elections from the Rampur seat but lost. Akash Saxena is a businessman by profession and the son of former minister Shiv Bahadur Saxena. So far, he has been directly involved as a complainant or party in 43 cases against Azam Khan.

stories.title: Threat to jobs of 1.86 lakh UP teachers deferred:SC grants more time to clear TET; August 31, 2028, set as final deadline
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has extended the time limit for teachers to clear the TET (Teacher Eligibility Test) by one year. Teachers will now have to qualify TET by August 31, 2028. Earlier, the last date was fixed as August 31, 2027. A division bench led by Justice Dipankar Datta delivered the verdict after hearing several review petitions. However, the court once again rejected petitions seeking exemption for all teachers appointed before 2009 from the mandatory TET requirement. The court said that all teachers working across the country must clear TET by August 31, 2028. In such a situation, the jobs of 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh still remain under threat in the TET mandatory case. On May 13, the court had told teachers seeking relief: Do not be selfish and think only about protecting your jobs, but also consider the children who need quality education. The court made the strict remark while hearing several petitions filed by the governments of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, along with teacher associations from West Bengal and Kerala, opposing the mandatory TET requirement. These petitions sought a review of the Supreme Court’s September 2025 judgment, which had directed all working teachers teaching Classes 1 to 8 in non-minority schools across the country to clear the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) within two years. At that time, the bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Manmohan had reserved its verdict after hearing the review petitions. How the TET issue became complicated Parliament passed the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act (RTE-2009) on August 4, 2009. It was implemented across the country from April 1, 2010. The objective of this law was to provide free and compulsory education to every child between 6 and 14 years of age from Classes 1 to 8. The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) made it mandatory for teachers to clear TET. On July 27, 2011, an order was issued making TET a compulsory service condition for recruitment at the primary and upper primary levels. On September 1, 2025, the Supreme Court bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Manmohan delivered a major verdict. The court said: All such teachers who have more than five years of service remaining must clear TET within two years (by September 2027). Those who have less than five years of service remaining have been exempted. However, even they will have to clear TET for promotions. Along with this, the bench also raised questions over the 2014 Karnataka-based Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust judgment, which had granted complete exemption from the RTE Act to minority institutions (aided or unaided). The court said the judgment required review, and the matter was referred to a constitutional bench. Jobs of 1.86 lakh UP teachers under threat Since the Supreme Court’s order, 21 lakh teachers across the country have been protesting. Among them are 1.86 lakh teachers from Uttar Pradesh. Many teachers have been teaching for 20 to 25 years. They argue that asking them to appear for an examination again after such long service is unreasonable. Teacher associations claim that two teachers have even died due to stress linked to the issue. Amid the teachers’ protest, the Uttar Pradesh government had filed a review petition before the Supreme Court’s division bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, on which the decision was delivered on Friday. TET must be cleared by August 31, 2028 Following the Supreme Court’s decision, the jobs of thousands of primary teachers across the country have come under threat. The court has made it clear that clearing TET will be mandatory to continue in service and to receive promotions. Now, according to the Supreme Court’s order, 1.86 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh will have to clear TET within three years, that is, by August 31, 2028. If teachers fail to clear TET within the stipulated time, they may have to leave their jobs or could be compulsorily retired. However, teachers who have only five years of service left have been given relief. But even they will have to clear TET to become eligible for promotions. TET examination scheduled in July The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission had announced the schedule for primary and upper primary level examinations on March 20. In Uttar Pradesh, the examination is going to be conducted after four years. Earlier, the application process for the examination had started in 2021, but the examination could only be held in 2022. This time, 15 to 20 lakh applicants may appear for the examination. This includes 1.86 lakh teachers who are currently working in council schools without having cleared TET.
