stories.title: Vinesh Phogat cleared to compete in 50kg Asian Games trials:Wrestler receives relief from Supreme Court after WFI controversy
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has allowed Olympian wrestler Vinesh Phogat to participate in the Asian Games trials. Yesterday (28 May), WFI (Wrestling Federation of India) had filed a petition in the Supreme Court to stop the trials, which was rejected by a bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe. However, Phogat has been granted clearance to compete only in the 50kg category trials. These trials are to be held in Delhi on 30 and 31 May. Based on the performance in these trials, players will be selected for the Asian Games to be held in Japan in September. The Delhi High Court, in its order dated May 22, had allowed Vinesh Phogat to participate in the selection trials. WFI had challenged this decision in the Supreme Court. The High Court had directed that the entire trial process be video recorded. To make it transparent, it should be conducted under the supervision of independent observers appointed by the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and the Indian Olympic Association (IOA). Vinesh Phogat had received relief from the Delhi High Court Earlier, a division bench of Delhi High Court Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Kariya had ruled in favor of Vinesh. The court was hearing Vinesh Phogat's appeal challenging the interim order of the single bench. The single-judge bench had refused to grant interim relief on her petition.favour Vinesh Phogat had challenged WFI's selection policy and the show-cause notice issued to her in her petition. However, the wrestler has only received the allowance for the 50kg category trails. According to WFI sources, federation officials waited for confirmation on her preferred weight division after the Supreme Court paved the way for her participation in Saturday's trials, but did not receive any communication from the two-time World Championship medallist till late Friday evening. : BCCI bans smart sunglasses in IPL:Board warns of strict action in case of violation, RR manager was fined earlier for using smartphone WFI on Vinesh Phogat's participation in the trials According to the PTI report, a WFI source said, “It is important for the chief coach and the technical officials to know which wrestler is competing in which weight category. We waited till late evening, but no email, message or any formal intimation was received from Vinesh's side.” It has been learnt that the celebrated wrestler has been preparing to compete in the 53kg class and was training at the Indira Gandhi Stadium complex here, which is also the venue for the trials. Further, a senior WFI official said that the federation would comply with the court's directions but conduct trials according to their own regulations. "Honouring the court orders, we will allow Vinesh to compete. But only WFI rules will apply during the competition. We have no objection if observers from the Indian Olympic Association and the Sports Ministry are present. In fact, we welcome their presence even as the Supreme Court has not passed any such direction. It was the High Court which had mentioned observers," the official said. Last match played at 2024 Paris Olympics Vinesh Phogat played her last wrestling match at the Paris Olympics in 2024. Vinesh played three matches in the 50kg weight category on 6 August, 2024, all on the same day. She defeated Cuban wrestler Yusneylis Guzman Lopez in the semi-finals. Before playing the final, her weight was checked and found to be 100 grams over. Following this, she was disqualified. Vinesh Phogat announced her retirement from wrestling on 8 August, 2024. On 12 December, 2025, Vinesh announced her return from retirement, stating that she wants to participate in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Vinesh is a Congress MLA from the Julana seat in Jind district of Haryana. Know the full controversy in a chronology Wrestling Federation had imposed a ban citing anti-doping rules WFI had disqualified Phogat from participating in domestic competitions until 26 June, 2026, citing the mandatory six-month notice period for athletes returning from retirement under anti-doping rules. A show-cause notice was also issued on charges of indiscipline and violation of anti-doping rules. The Wrestling Federation had written - Vinesh did not give six months' notice for her return from retirement. This violated the WFI constitution, United World Wrestling (UWW) rules, and anti-doping provisions. WFI further stated that her behaviour damaged the image of Indian wrestling and caused national embarrassment. It also sought a response from Vinesh on four major charges and asked why action should not be taken. On WFI's ban, Vinesh posted a video and said these things Was away from the wrestling mat for the last one and a half years Posting a video on social media, Vinesh said - Hello everyone. As everyone knows, I have been quite far from the wrestling mat for the last one and a half years. But now, for a few months, I have been preparing for wrestling. I am working with great hard work and honesty. Just as I won medals for the country before, with the blessings of God and your cooperation, I want to go back to the wrestling mat and win many medals for the country and uphold the honour of the country's tricolour. Competition Announced a Month Ago Vinesh further said that she wanted to share some things with everyone through a video. About a month ago, the Wrestling Federation announced a competition. This tournament is being organised in Gonda, UP, where Brijbhushan's house is. There is his private college. For every hardworking player to get their due, this is highly unlikely and impossible. Government Left Everything to Brijbhushan's Discretion Vinesh said, "Which referee will go to whose match? Which referee will give how many points? Which match chairman will sit where? Who is to be made to win, who is to be made to lose? All this will be controlled by Brijbhushan and his people. The government and our Sports Ministry are watching this as silent spectators." No one is coming forward to help the players, as if Brijbhushan has been given a free hand to do whatever he wants. Whether you do something with women wrestlers or anything with the wrestling world. We stand with you. I don't think that the weight of all hardworking players will be checked properly, and the real result of their hard work will come out on the mat. Case pending in court for three years Vinesh said that three years ago today, we had also raised our voice against sexual harassment. The related case is pending in court. 6 women players had filed a complaint and given testimony in it, and testimonies are ongoing in that case. It is a guideline of the Supreme Court that the identity of any victim should not be made public, as it concerns their dignity and self-respect. Today, there are some compulsions that I want to tell you all something. I didn't want to speak right now, because the case is pending in court. All the truth will come out before the country. I want to tell you that I am one of those 6 victims who filed the complaint. Vinesh Phogat and the sexual harassment case Accusations of sexual harassment against Brijbhushan On 18 January 2023, wrestlers Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik, and Bajrang Punia staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi, accusing Brijbhushan of sexually harassing female wrestlers. Vinesh Phogat, crying, said - Brijbhushan Sharan Singh and coaches sexually harass female wrestlers in the national camp. Brijbhushan used to stay in the players' hotel, which is against the rules. After the defeat in the Tokyo Olympics, the WFI president called me a bad coin. : Hardik Pandya to lose Mumbai captaincy, team spot in jeopardy:Dents in MI camp as coaching staff calls seniors 'uncoachable' post season-exit Brijbhushan had said - if the allegations are proven true, I will hang myself On these allegations, former Wrestling Federation president Brijbhushan had clarified, saying, ‘There has been no harassment of any kind. If it has happened, I will hang myself. He called the protest sponsored and attributed it to Haryana Congress Rajya Sabha MP Deepender Hooda. He had said that these players are no longer fit to play even at the national level.’

stories.title: Yogi says mafia can no longer threaten Hindus openly:Targets SP over lawlessness, warns criminals in Mau
stories.summary: In a blistering attack on the Samajwadi Party, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday accused the previous government of shielding mafia elements, blocking welfare schemes and allowing lawlessness to flourish across the state. Addressing a public gathering in Madhuban, Mau, he said the BJP government had transformed the state's security environment and ensured that public welfare schemes reached the poor. The Chief Minister inaugurated and laid the foundation stone of 114 development projects worth Rs 392 crore. Although he was scheduled to arrive at 9.30 am, bad weather delayed his visit by around 30 minutes. Cabinet ministers, including Om Prakash Rajbhar and A. K. Sharma, shared the stage with him. He said- The previous government bowed before the mafia. There was anarchy and chaos. Now I can say that no mafia or goon has the audacity to create disturbance during any festival. If anyone disrupts any religious event, the festival will be celebrated, but their fate will be sealed like Ravana and Kansa. Read 5 major points from CM Yogi's speech... 1- An attempt was made to burn Mau 21 years ago CM Yogi said, “Those who are older than 30-35 years here will remember that in 2005, 21 years ago, a vicious attempt was made to burn this very Mau. How the power mafia was creating disturbances in a festive center of faith, the Ramlila event, and committing atrocities on the innocent.” The government was bowing down before the mafia. The security here was in danger. There was a rampage of lawlessness. Development works were not happening, but when funds were collected and some religious event was organized somewhere, it was not allowed to take place. Obstacles were created in it. 2- Daughters were being abducted in broad daylight The CM said, "Daughters could not go to school, hooligans used to harass them. Abductions would happen at any time. Traders were forced to close their shops before sunset. If any family member did not reach home after sunset, the family would become worried about what might happen to them, In that riot-like atmosphere, in an atmosphere full of lawlessness, a crisis of identity had emerged before the youth here. There were no jobs in the state. But when they went outside the state, people would step back 10 paces upon hearing the name of UP." 3- SP government used to bow down before the mafia Yogi said- Earlier there was no facility for the poor. You handed over the reins of the country to Narendra Modi in 2014. In the last 12 years you have seen a changing India. Modi ji says there are only 4 castes for us. One caste of the poor, one of the youth, one of women and one of the farmer who feeds us. If you recall, everyone is included in these four. If these four are uplifted, the country will start running. Modi ji used to make plans in Delhi, but from 2014 to 2017, the Samajwadi Party government in UP did not let them be implemented in the state. SP did nothing for the poor. The SP government used to grovel before the mafia. They would break into a sweat, couldn't even speak in front of the mafia. 4- Goons would swallow the rations meant for the poor The CM said - Those who are going around preaching today, they should be asked why the 65 lakh houses that have been given to the poor were not given during the SP government. SP had government 4 times, why weren't toilets built then. Congress ruled for 50 years, why didn't they do it. Why didn't the poor get rations then. In both their governments, goons would swallow the rations. Today, 100 million people in the state have been given free healthcare facilities. Every farmer and poor person will get this facility. 5- Those who will harm daughter will go to ‘Yamraj’ The CM said - Now if anyone stops religious events, their fate will be like Kansa and Ravana. If anyone breaches the security of daughters and traders, only Yamraj will be waiting, no one else. Today, a mafia cannot threaten any Hindu by roaming in an open jeep brandishing a pistol. OP Rajbhar and AK Sharma were present on the stage On stage were Cabinet Minister Omprakash Rajbhar, Jail Minister Dara Singh Chauhan, Energy Minister AK Sharma, District In-charge Minister Girish Chand Yadav, BJP MLA from Madhuban Assembly Ram Vilas Chauhan, MLC Vikrant Singh Rishu, MLC Bichelal Rajbhar, former MLA Vijay Rajbhar, former MLA Umesh Chand Pandey were also present. OP Rajbhar predicts SP will meet a bad fate in 2027 Minister Omprakash Rajbhar said that today we are the Panchayati Raj Minister. In Chandauli, SP's own leaders beat a female SP leader. 5 people from the Yadav community go and beat the woman by grabbing her hair, where did socialism go. In Barabanki, these socialist people slit the throat of a youth from the Rajbhar community for asking for ice cream money. Akhilesh says democracy is being murdered, this murder is being committed by SP itself. The fate that befell SP in 2017, an even worse fate will befall it in 2027.

stories.title: ATS arrests 4 terror suspects in UP:Video calls in Urdu-Punjabi exposed Pakistan-linked module; BJP offices, hospitals were among targets
stories.summary: The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) and Special Task Force (STF) arrested 4 suspected terrorists of a Pakistani terror module from Saharanpur, UP. They were conspiring to carry out blasts at several sensitive locations, including BJP offices, hospitals, and schools. Among them, 2 suspects, Mahkab and Shahrukh, are residents of Saharanpur. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to their families and villagers in Saharanpur. A villager said - Mahkab used to sit with everyone in the evening earlier. Then gradually, he started living separately from everyone. He didn't talk much to anyone. He used his mobile late into the night. He used to talk in Punjabi or Urdu on video calls. His conversations were not easily understood. If someone passed by while he was talking, he would turn his face away. Meanwhile, Shahrukh's mother, crying, said - "My son has been wrongly framed. We taught him to earn and live through hard work." Villagers also said - "He was very friendly. He had no quarrels with anyone." The same boys whom we used to see roaming in the fields and making reels on mobile phones until yesterday, are now reported to be linked to a terrorist network. ATS investigation revealed that the suspects befriended the network of Pakistani gangsters Shahzad Bhatti and Aakib Jatt through Instagram. Orders were given via video calls. Conversations took place in codewords. First, know about the four suspected terrorists Mahakab slowly distanced himself from the villagers Dhikka Kala village is located in the Sarsawa area, about 30 km from Saharanpur district headquarters. On the morning of May 27 (Wednesday), police, intelligence agencies, and media suddenly gathered in the village. That's when people learned about Mahakab's terrorist connection. When we reached Dhikka Kala village, Mahakab's father, Hasrat, was lying dejected on a cot outside his house. When we asked, he said, "My son used to work as a welder in Punjab. When he came home, he would help with farming. We never had any suspicion." The family is involved in farming. We have about 10 bighas of land. The house is normal, and the family has no criminal history. Villagers also say about Mahakab that he was of a quiet nature. However, in the last few months, he started spending more time on his mobile. Shahrukh's mother cried and said - My son has been framed The atmosphere at the house of the second suspected terrorist, Shahrukh, was also tense. His mother, crying, could only say - "My son used to work installing tiles in Dehradun. We are poor people. How would we know who does what on Instagram? My son has been wrongly framed." "Our son is not like that. We taught him to earn and live through hard work. My son has been framed." Shahrukh's family owns 11-12 bighas of land. According to villagers, he was sociable and never got into any fights. Teacher said - not poor by money, but mentally empty A large number of youths from Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, and Haridwar belt go to Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttarakhand for labor work. The lives of most youths are now shrinking between mobile phones and social media. In conversations on the ground, one thing repeatedly emerged: these youths have neither stable employment nor a clear direction for the future. A local teacher says - these boys are not very poor economically, but they are mentally empty. Social media has become their world. If someone calls them 'brother' on Instagram, shows them dreams of money and foreign lands, they are quickly influenced. Then they fall into the clutches of terrorists. Radical networks are now working on a 'digital friendship model' instead of direct religious speeches. First friendship, then emotional connection, then confidential chats, and finally connecting them to the network this is the new strategy. Farmer said - Earlier the fear was of bad company, now it's of mobile phones In Dhikka Kala village, the only discussion in every household now is whether social media has become a path to terror in villages? Mahkab and Shahrukh's family members say that they never imagined that their children could be in contact with such a network. The village elders are now expressing concern over children's mobile usage. An elderly farmer said - Earlier the fear was of bad company, of getting trapped in addiction. Now the fear is of mobile phones. Terrorist network showed suspects dreams of a lavish life ATS investigation has revealed that Mahkab and Gagandeep's friendship was formed through Instagram with the network of Pakistani gangsters Shahzad Bhatti and Akib Jatt. It started with normal chatting. Then video calls started coming. Gradually, the conversation progressed to work. Initially, these youths were sent social media posts, religious videos, and content related to injustice. Then they were shown dreams of fighting against the system and a lavish life. They were also lured with money and weapons. Later, they were asked to conduct reconnaissance of hospitals, BJP offices, and sensitive locations. They were also ordered to connect as many young people as possible to the network. Orders were given via video calls. Codewords were used in conversations, and Instagram accounts were frequently changed. ADG said - The four had a meeting in Noida ADG Law and Order Amitabh Yash said - Pakistani gangster Akib Jatt had also asked the four via video call to recruit as many people as possible to carry out terrorist incidents at several places in the country. Mehkab and Gagandeep had recruited Shahrukh and Musharraf. Among these four, there was talk on social media about reconnaissance for blowing up hospitals and purchasing weapons. To carry out a major incident in March 2026, Mehkab and Gagandeep had a meeting in Noida. In the meeting, there was talk between them about obtaining money and weapons. A conspiracy for hand grenade attacks was being hatched in Western UP According to ATS, the suspects were tasked with reconnoitering BJP offices, hospitals, and some business establishments. It also emerged during interrogation that a conspiracy for hand grenade attacks was being hatched in several places in Western UP. Weapons and explosives are suspected to be supplied from POK. Agencies are now investigating which places these youths reconnoitered in UP. Due to Sarsawa Airbase and Army Area in Saharanpur, the investigation has become even more sensitive. They were not only moving towards radicalization themselves, but were also recruiting other youths. New recruits were being sought through social media. Now unemployed are targets of terrorists, recruitment strategy changed Officials of security agencies say that terrorist networks are now working on a 'low visibility model'. They are choosing youths who do not easily come under the radar of security agencies. Until a few years ago, the strategy of terrorist organizations and Pakistan-backed networks was different. They used to try to trap educated, technically knowledgeable, high-profile, and influential youth in their net. Doctors, engineering students, IT professionals, and highly educated youth were trained through radical ideologies. Now, the new targets of terrorists are laborers from small towns, unemployed youth, boys working in fields, and the poor generation spending hours on social media. The story of the 4 youths arrested from Saharanpur is considered the biggest indicator of this changing strategy. Now, know Shahzad Bhatti... According to the investigation by the Special Cell of Delhi Police, Indian intelligence and law enforcement agencies have identified Pakistan-based gangster-turned-terrorists Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt as the alleged masterminds of the recently emerged organisation Tehrik-e-Taliban Hindustan (TTH). Shahzad Bhatti and gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, who is imprisoned in Sabarmati Jail in Gujarat, were once good friends. However, after Bhatti used Lawrence's henchmen for his work and Lawrence's threat to Hafiz Saeed over the Pahalgam attack, they became sworn enemies. Lawrence is originally from Fazilka, Punjab. He studied at Punjab University in Chandigarh. Subsequently, several cases like murder and extortion were registered against him. More than 12 suspects caught in 2 months In the last two months in UP, agencies have caught more than 12 suspected terrorists. On April 4, 4 suspects were caught from Lucknow. During ATS interrogation, it was revealed that they had an offer from Pakistan: "You people spread terror, the more terror, the more money you will get...". In an attempt to carry out a major blast, the four suspected terrorists rehearsed by setting a pickup truck and a bike on fire. Its videos were sent to Pakistani handler Abu Bakar. In return, they received 12 thousand rupees for each arson incident. After this, ATS arrested 2 more suspects, Tushar from Meerut and Sameer Khan from Delhi, on April 24. Both were in contact with Pakistani gangsters Shahzad Bhatti and Abid Jatt. According to ATS, both were planning to kill ex-Muslims in UP with hand grenades. They were lured with 3 lakh rupees for target killing.

stories.title: Gorakhpur awaits Amrit Bharat trains:Railway Board allocates two new sleeper rakes, services for Mumbai and Delhi likely to begin
stories.summary: A major boost for rail passengers in eastern Uttar Pradesh could be just around the corner. Gorakhpur is likely to receive two sleeper rakes of the Amrit Bharat Express after the Railway Board allocated them to the North Eastern Railway. Railway sources indicate that both rakes may arrive in Gorakhpur on Friday, paving the way for the launch of new Amrit Bharat services to Delhi and Mumbai. The development is being seen as a significant step towards easing pressure on two of the busiest long-distance routes originating from the region. New services planned for Delhi and Mumbai Every day, thousands of passengers travel from Gorakhpur to Delhi and Mumbai for employment, education, business and medical treatment. Demand on both routes remains consistently high throughout the year, leaving many travellers struggling to secure confirmed tickets. With the arrival of the new rakes, railway authorities are expected to begin operational preparations for launching dedicated Amrit Bharat trains on these routes. The proposed services are expected to offer: Securing a confirmed berth on trains bound for Delhi and Mumbai has become increasingly difficult, especially during festivals, school vacations and holiday seasons. Passengers often face lengthy waiting lists, forcing many to postpone travel plans or seek alternative transport. Railway officials believe the addition of new Amrit Bharat trains will help address this long-standing issue by increasing the number of available seats. The move is expected to reduce congestion and improve travel convenience for regular commuters and occasional travellers alike. Benefits likely across the Purvanchal region The impact of the new trains will extend well beyond Gorakhpur city. Gorakhpur Junction serves as a major railway hub for several neighbouring districts, making it a critical transport lifeline for eastern Uttar Pradesh. Passengers from the following districts are expected to benefit: For many residents, the proposed trains could mean easier and more reliable access to Delhi and Mumbai. Capacity increase expected to be significant According to the railway's initial plan, the operation of both Amrit Bharat trains could provide additional travel facilities to nearly 3,200 passengers every day. The expected increase in capacity is likely to bring considerable relief on routes that regularly witness heavy passenger demand throughout the year. Official announcement awaited While the allocation of the rakes has raised expectations among travellers, railway authorities are currently completing the necessary formalities before launching the services. For now, passengers are eagerly awaiting an official announcement. If the process moves as expected, Gorakhpur could soon gain two much-needed trains that promise to make long-distance travel smoother, faster and more accessible for thousands across the region every day.

stories.title: Varanasi Mayor’s claims exposed after rain:Azad Park area turns into a pond, roads submerged in filth; affected share their ordeal
stories.summary: Heavy rain and thunderstorms that swept through Varanasi and adjoining districts early Friday morning laid bare the Municipal Corporation’s claims on drainage and monsoon preparedness. The spell of rain once again exposed the ground reality behind repeated assurances made by Mayor Ashok Tiwari and civic authorities. The impact was visible in Azad Park of the Kachibagh ward, where rainwater accumulated across roads and public spaces, forcing residents to wade through waterlogged stretches. Commuters and local residents faced considerable inconvenience as the area resembled a flooded pocket of the city. Residents said the problem has persisted for years despite repeated complaints to the authorities. According to them, every spell of rain leads to severe waterlogging, while the receding water leaves behind thick layers of mud and filth, making movement difficult and raising concerns over sanitation. To verify the civic body's claims, Dainik Bhaskar visited Azad Park shortly after the rain. Conversations with residents revealed a long-standing pattern of neglect, with locals questioning why a chronic problem continues to resurface despite repeated promises of permanent solutions.. Read the report... See pictures of waterlogging... Now, know what the Mayor said on completing three years of his tenure? Held press conference on three years of tenure On Tuesday, May 26, at the Smart City auditorium, Mayor Ashok Tiwari had enumerated the achievements of his three-year tenure at Varanasi Municipal Corporation. During this, he had talked about completing sewer cleaning before the rains at any cost and had also claimed that there would be no waterlogging anywhere in the city. ‘We have no control over nature’ When journalists said that news like "rain exposes municipal corporation" gets published, he said bluntly - you will definitely publish the news; before the arrival of rain, the municipal corporation is cleaning drains and pits in all corporation areas. Cleaning of sewers is ongoing. So that there is no problem of water logging anywhere during the rainy season. In the recent rain in Varanasi's corporation area, water logging occurred only at Girjaghar. Because construction is going on there. Otherwise, Trauma Center and Cantonment area where water logging happens. All those places are outside our officers' jurisdiction. We are doing as much as possible. But it's nature. We have no control over it. Rain exposed the reality But this claim was exposed by the heavy rain that occurred in Varanasi on May 29, when severe water logging was seen in Azad Park in Kachibag ward of the city. The rain stopped at 7 AM but till 12 noon, the water in this area had not drained and people were forced to move through sewage water. Know what the people living in Azad Park and its surrounding areas said... Problem remains the same despite complaint to Lucknow Imran Ali, a resident of Azad Park area, said - When it rains, water accumulates here completely. The rainwater doesn't drain immediately. We face problems for 8 to 10 hours. We have complained about this to Lucknow many times. We had complained to Lucknow even a day before Bakrid, but no cleaning was done. The cleaning post is right next door but they don't care and the employees rest in the post. When the water drains, they will do a little cleaning and sit back in the post. It's a festival day but there is no hearing. Seeing the problem since gaining consciousness Ahmad Hussain said, “My house is right on Azad Park. Whether it rains lightly or heavily, water fills up to our house. There is difficulty in living and commuting. There is a sanitation post near our house but no one solves the problem. We have been seeing this problem since we gained consciousness.” ‘Municipal Corporation is lying’ Hussain exposed the Mayor's claims by saying that the Municipal Corporation was lying. If there is no water logging anywhere in the city, then what is this? If that were the case, water would not be visible here either. In such a situation, they should work on the ground rather than lie. If it rains more, water won't drain the whole day Ansar Ahmed said, “When it rains a little, water accumulates here. If it rains for one hour, water stays for four to five hours and if it rains more, the whole day passes in draining the water. It's a festival day but there is no hearing. The water problem here is quite old but there is no solution.”

stories.title: SP MLA Naseem faces ₹3 crore extortion allegations:She denies charges, claims traders were being illegally charged goat market fees
stories.summary: SP MLA Naseem Solanki has rejected all allegations made against her husband, Irfan Solanki in the Kanpur goat market dispute. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the Sisamau MLA claimed that illegal money was being collected from traders in the name of market fees. Naseem Solanki said, “₹500 was being charged for bringing a goat to the market, and another ₹100 was being taken as entry fee. There was no fair there. To know the truth, I went there with my husband, Irfan and a gunner. I stayed in the car while my husband and the gunner entered the market with 8-10 people.” She alleged that goat market operator Wafa Abbas gathered around 150 people and created tension at the spot. “Why was the market gate closed? Does he think he is such a big goon? He wants to get me and my husband killed,” she said. The controversy started after Wafa Abbas filed a police case against Irfan Solanki, accusing him of assault, abuse and issuing threats. Abbas alleged that Irfan demanded ₹3 lakh in the name of allowing the market to operate. When he objected, he was allegedly beaten up. He also claimed that ₹2.70 lakh was looted from his gunman. Meanwhile, Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal has suspended MLA Gunner Azeem Ahmed. According to the Commissioner, the gunman neglected his duty by entering the market premises instead of staying with the MLA for her security. 500 rupees were being charged for taking one goat SP MLA Naseem Solanki said, "Due to the crowd, I remained seated in the car some distance from the ground, while Irfan, elder son Mustafa, gunman Azeem Ahmed, and others went to the market. A little later, my son called and informed me not to come here, as a fight had broken out. I got ready to go to the spot." But, my son said, "Don't come, there's a lot of commotion happening here." Fearing an attack on the car, I left the place. When I learned the reality of the whole matter, I found out that the people present there (Wafa Abbas) had created an atmosphere of chaos. Despite recognizing my husband, he behaved rudely. He took Irfan Solanki's name and said, "Get out of the way." His tone was so rude that it seemed as if he was herding everyone with the same stick. 150 people brought in to spoil the atmosphere According to Naseem Solanki, Irfan told him to talk calmly, asking what had happened. After this, he also misbehaved with our gunner. When the gunner protested, Wafa Abbas said, "Just because you are a policeman, does that mean we will be scared of you?" At this, an argument started between the two. Shoving began. Irfan was with 8 to 10 people. He brought 100-150 people and suddenly spoiled the atmosphere there, starting slogans and pushing, and tried to get all the market gates closed. MLA Naseem Solanki said, "What did he ultimately want to do by closing the gate? Is he such a big goon? Is he the owner of Haleem College? He (Wafa Abbas) stated in his statement that I respectfully asked the MLA to move, which is completely false. I was listening on the phone, and despite recognizing Irfan, he was continuously abusing him." Naseem said - Those who make allegations should be ashamed On the accusation of 3 lakh extortion and robbery, Naseem said that those who make such accusations should be ashamed, what would a policeman snatch money for? Everyone knows he has such a good history himself. On the question of threat to Wafa Abbas's life, MLA Naseem Solanki sarcastically said, "Is his life in danger? I have heard that he has been charged under a section that could endanger our lives. His history indicates that my husband and I are in danger from him." She said, "This is not a laughing matter, he should be ashamed. On one hand, he is shouting that I made Irfan Solanki contest the election, and on the other hand, he is claiming a threat to his life. I want to make one thing clear to him: there is no threat to his life from my side. I also went to meet the Police Commissioner. I apprised him of the entire incident, including information about the illegal extortion case in Halim Maidan." Now read what Wafa Abbas says, who filed an FIR against Irfan Solanki Wafa Abbas, the goat market operator, stated in the complaint filed at Chamanganj police station in Kanpur: Irfan Solanki's gunman pushed him and slapped him. During this, Irfan stood by as a spectator. If he had shown impartiality and separated everyone, this issue would not have escalated so much. Wafa Abbas stated that he has been operating the goat market held at Halim College ground for about 6 years. It was around 1 AM on Tuesday night, and the market was crowded with customers and cattle traders for Eid al-Adha. During this time, former SP MLA Irfan Solanki arrived with his gunman Azeem Ahmed and some other people, with a full entourage. Irfan Solanki was standing with his companions at the main gate of the market ground. We told his gunman Azeem Ahmed to stand aside with the former MLA, as animals and vehicles were coming into the market, so that they wouldn't get hurt. Irfan Solanki did not stop the gunman even once Wafa Abbas said that as soon as he heard this, the gunner became ready to fight, he pushed me and slapped me. When I and my colleague Fahad protested, the gunner started slapping me one after another. The gunner started snatching my bag. I don't know if a lot of money fell from my bag during the snatching or if the gunner took it. In this whole matter, Irfan Solanki did not say a single word, nor did he stop the gunner, even though we used to be with him in every election. How is Irfan roaming with the MLA's wife's gunner? Wafa Abbas said- Police should investigate how Irfan is roaming with a gunman when Irfan's wife, SP MLA Naseem Solanki, has been provided with a gunman. The FIR filed by the gunman states the time as 12 PM on Wednesday morning, whereas the entire incident took place on Tuesday night. Gunman Azeem is misleading the administration. The Police Commissioner should investigate this entire matter. The gunman is working to defame the police administration. My entire dispute was with the gunman. A complaint was filed against the gunman, but his name is not in the FIR, why was this done? Wafa Abbas stated that she had filed a complaint of extortion and robbery, but there is no trace of it. How was a case registered under assault charges, when my purse was snatched, and money was taken? I have 100 witnesses, which should be investigated. The gunman had also committed assault at another place before. I am being called a criminal; it should be investigated who committed the crime, who ruined people's homes? stories.title: Temple-mosque row erupts in Lucknow village:Hindu groups call it Maharaja Kansa Pasi fort; police seal disputed shrin after tensions rise
stories.summary: Kasamandi Kalan town is located in Malihabad, Lucknow. The atmosphere around a tomb and mosque here is heated these days. The Hindu side claims that this is the fort of Maharaja Kansa Pasi. There was a Shiva temple in one part of it, which was converted into a mazar (shrine). The basis of this claim is the figures of snakes, flowers, and kalash (urns) on the walls. Meanwhile, Muslims claim- There has been a mazar here for 850 years and a mosque for 250 years. We have been offering prayers for many years. Amidst these claims, local people say - there was no dispute here until 2 years ago. No one used to come to offer prayers. After that, people started coming to offer prayers. Now the dispute has escalated. To maintain law and order, the police have sealed the disputed site. Neither Muslim devotees can offer prayers, nor can Hindus recite Hanuman Chalisa. A company of PAC has been deployed. The roads leading to the disputed structure have been sealed. Where did the controversy begin? Issue arose after former Deputy CM's statement This dates back 8 months. On September 28, 2025, Dinesh Sharma, former UP Deputy CM and current Rajya Sabha MP, attended the Maharaja Kansa Pasi Mahotsav. This event was held in Kasamandi, Malihabad. At that time, he had said- The Mughals and the British made every possible effort to defame the Pasi community. They feared that the Pasi community could end their rule. Lucknow and its surrounding areas used to belong to Pasi kings. History mentions 4 generations of Maharaja Kansa Pasi. In the meeting, it was also discussed why there is no historical heritage associated with someone who ruled for 4 generations. Where is their fort? Where are the things related to them? After this, several organisations became active. Leading the way was 'Lakhan Army'. Suraj Pasi is its chief. Suraj Pasi of Bholapur, Lucknow, formed the Lakhan Ekta Mission on February 27, 2023. Later, its name was changed to Lakhan Army. Claim - Fort, with a Shiva temple in one part of it The fresh controversy started around May 20. Several organizations, including Lakhan Army and Hindu Mahasabha, announced that this was the fort of Maharaja Kansa Pasi. There is an ancient Shiva temple in one part of it, and we will worship here. After this, the administration became active. Discussions also started among the Muslim side. The effect of this was that on May 22, on the day of Juma (Friday prayers), a large number of Muslim people reached this place to offer prayers, whereas earlier only 10-15 people used to offer prayers. Lakhan Army chief Suraj Pasi says- The plate they have installed on top of the structure was recently installed with cement. Whereas, the walls are made of Lakhuri bricks and lime. Similarly, the shrine inside is made of cement. You would not have seen anything like this anywhere, because it is just a figure. Besides, look at the interior design, signs of Naga civilization are visible. Naga (serpent), flowers, kalash (pot), and traditional Hindu figures are made, which do not match Islamic architecture in any way. Suraj says - they have encroached here. Besides this, a 12-foot shrine has also been built 300 meters away. That belongs to our King Pasi Kansa, but these people claim that place as their own too. There are no Hindu monuments here. Muslims have tried to erase a 1000-year-old civilization here. We tell CM Yogi to bring the bulldozer here as well. No namaz was offered until 2 years ago Kasamandi Kala is a Hindu-majority area. In the place where this disputed structure is located, about 30% are Muslims, and the rest of the population is Hindu. A woman from here says - We have been here for 10 years. Earlier, after bathing, we used to light incense sticks. But, for the past 2 years, Namaz (prayer) has started here. Those who offer Namaz are Shia people; they come from Lucknow. It's not our place, so we never went to ask. Another 70-year-old Hindu woman says - We have been living here for 50 years. For 2 years, people from outside have started coming to offer Namaz. We don't go there anymore. Hindu people also never performed any worship here; this place just remained as it was. The local Muslim people here go to the nearby mosque to offer Namaz. Now, what the dispute is about, we have no information regarding that. Controversy escalated due to the plaque on top of the tomb There is a plaque on top of the tomb. The entire structure is made of limestone, but this marble plaque has been separately affixed with cement. It looks like it might have been installed 1 or 2 years ago. It mentions an incident from the year 1246 in Persian. In it, a father has written a message on the death of his 11-year-old daughter. Its Hindi translation is - My little daughter left the world at a young age, my heart is distressed by the grief of her departure. People from the Pasi community, who are protesting, say - merely installing a Persian plaque does not change the original history of a place. This is the fort of Maharaja Kansa Pasi from the 11th century. That is why a memorandum has been given to the SDM and DM to get this place investigated by the Archaeological Department. Woman's body prevented from going to graveyard On May 26, numerous workers of the Hindu Mahasabha arrived at the disputed site with the insistence of performing puja. The police stopped them. After this, their memorandum was taken. People from the Hindu Mahasabha announced that they would perform puja and recite Hanuman Chalisa at the disputed site on the day of Bakrid. Just one day later, the administration ordered that no one would go near the disputed site on Bakrid. Neither namaz would be offered nor any kind of puja would be performed. This strictness was evident on the occasion of Bakrid, and no one could reach the disputed site. This dispute is escalating. The place where the disputed site is located is registered as a graveyard in government records. On the night of May 27, a woman from the village died. People started taking the body towards the graveyard for burial. At this, a worker of Lakhan Army started protesting. Police personnel present at the spot took him into custody. Then the woman's last rites were performed in the same graveyard. Locally, the dispute has deepened further after this incident. Muslim side claims - only tomb and mosque are recorded in government records People from the Muslim side shy away from talking on camera. Jamal, a retired teacher from the village, says- Earlier, people from the Sunni community used to offer prayers here. Later, Shias started offering prayers. Prayers are offered here only on Fridays. If you look at the revenue records, this land is registered in the name of the Jama family. Their descendants settled abroad after migrating from the Asoha area of Unnao. There has never been any dispute here. Hindus and Muslims have always lived together. Another person says that both the mosque and the graveyard are mentioned in the records of the 1933 Fasli settlement and the 1359 Fasli land register. If the Archaeological Survey of India investigates this, the truth will be revealed. After that, the land should be given to whichever community owns it. Some people in the village hold different views from all this. They say - We do not support the construction of either a temple or a mosque here. We want a girls' school, a hospital, or a community marriage hall to be built here. This will benefit people from all sections of society.

stories.title: Former Haryana CM's Chief Secretary dies in AC blast incident:Son seriously injured; family belongs to UP
stories.summary: Dhanendra Kumar, who served as the Principal Secretary to former Haryana CM Chaudhary Bhajanlal, died in a fire. Dhanendra lived at his residence in Delhi after retirement. On Wednesday night, the AC installed in his house suddenly exploded. After the blast, the house caught fire. Within a short time, the fire engulfed the entire house. Dhanendra and his son also suffered burn injuries in the fire. The police team, upon receiving information, admitted them to the AIIMS Trauma Centre. He died early Thursday morning during treatment. Dhanendra was a 1967 batch IAS officer. After serving as the CM's Principal Secretary, he also held several important positions in the central government. Additionally, Dhanendra also served as an Executive Director at the World Bank. AC exploded, fire spread in the house Police officials said that on Wednesday night around 11 pm, they received information about a fire in the Hauz Khas area. Police and fire tenders reached the spot. During the rescue operation, everyone present in the house was barely brought out. However, Dhanendra and his son were seriously burnt in the accident. 5 people were present in the house Firefighters say that at the time of the incident, 5 people, including family members and a caretaker, were present in the house. Preliminary investigation has revealed that the fire started after an explosion in the air conditioner unit inside the house, which quickly engulfed the entire area. The police have recorded the statements of eyewitnesses. Further action will be taken after the technical report arrives. Was an officer of Haryana cadre Dhanendra Kumar Garg was a senior IAS officer of the 1967 batch from the Haryana cadre. He had a long and distinguished career in administrative service. He served as the Chief Secretary to the former CM of Haryana and later held several important responsibilities in the central government as well. He also served as the Chairman of the Competition Commission of India, Chairman of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), Telecom Secretary, held top positions related to GST, and was the Central Excise Commissioner. Was a resident of Saharanpur, UP Even after retirement, he remained associated with public life and served as Executive Director representing India at the World Bank. Dhanendra Kumar was a resident of Gangoh in Saharanpur district of Uttar Pradesh.

stories.title: Storms and rain lash UP during Nautapa heatwave:Winds touch 100 kmph in Lucknow-Prayagraj belt; hailstorm alert issued across 24 districts
stories.summary: Heavy rain and strong storms brought major weather changes across Uttar Pradesh on the fifth day of Nautapa on Friday. Lucknow and Prayagraj witnessed heavy rain and winds reaching 100 kmph early in the morning, while a hailstorm was reported in Saharanpur. In Jhansi, a unipole installed by the municipal corporation collapsed during the storm. Rain has continued in Varanasi since morning. The India Meteorological Department said the spell of rain may continue till May 31. An orange alert for rain has been issued in 24 districts, while storm warnings are in place across all 75 districts of the state. Rain had already started in several districts, including Ghaziabad, Mathura, Kasganj, Sambhal and Farrukhabad, late on Thursday evening. Dark clouds covered Meerut, while Shahjahanpur received rain after a dust storm. Earlier, a heavy hailstorm was also reported in Jhansi and Badaun. Despite the sudden change in weather, heatwave conditions remained severe in many areas on Thursday. Banda was the hottest city in the state with a temperature of 47.8°C. In Prayagraj, people were seen covering themselves while travelling to escape the scorching heat. In Ayodhya, a moving auto-rickshaw caught fire due to the extreme heat, forcing passengers to jump out to save their lives. See weather pictures- The picture is from Kaimganj, Farrukhabad. Here, the rain started after lightning struck. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Kumar Singh, said- A new Western Disturbance is becoming active from today. A cyclonic circulation is present at a height over South Bihar and surrounding areas. In such a situation, there may be rain with thunderstorms in the state. This can provide relief from the heat. The temperature may drop by 68C. Orange Alert for Hailstorm Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Mathura, Hathras, Etah, Agra, Firozabad, Mainpuri, Etawah, Auraiya, Bijnor, Amroha, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Jhansi. Storm with a speed of 60 to 80 km per hour Saharanpur, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Hapur, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Bulandshahr, Aligarh, Mathura, Hathras, Kasganj, Etah, Agra, Firozabad, Mainpuri, Etawah, Auraiya, Bijnor, Amroha, Moradabad, Rampur, Bareilly, Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, Sambhal, Badaun, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Jhansi. How will the weather be for the next 3 days?

stories.title: 6 labourers killed after bridge slab collapses in UP:Storm and heavy rain trigger incident at under construction Betwa river site
stories.summary: The slab of the under-construction bridge being built over the Betwa river in Hamirpur, UP, collapsed at 3 AM on Friday. 6 laborers died in the accident. Many laborers are still feared to be trapped. Currently, a rescue operation is underway at the site. Debris is being removed with a JCB. A team from the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) has also reached the spot. According to eyewitnesses, the slab fell due to a strong storm and rain, trapping the laborers working underneath. stories.title: 4-year-old girl dies after falling into well in Agra:Family questions delay in rescue operation and lack of oxygen
stories.summary: On Thursday in Agra, a 4-year-old girl, who had come to her grandfather's house, fell into a 70-foot deep well while playing. Upon receiving information, teams from the police, administration, and fire brigade reached the spot. However, due to poisonous gas and lack of oxygen in the well, the rescue operation became very difficult. During the nearly 4-hour long rescue operation, a fire brigade personnel descended into the well with an oxygen cylinder. After hours of struggle, the girl was pulled out and taken to the CHC (Community Health Center). However, doctors declared her dead. As soon as the news of the innocent child's death was received, the family was plunged into chaos. During the incident, people's anger also erupted at the scene. The father, holding the hand of SDM Vinod Kumar, screamed, 'There were only 4 people working on the rescue, what were the other 100-50 policemen doing there...? Bring back, my daughter... Bring back my daughter...'. Hearing the father's cries, the eyes of the people present at the scene welled up. See 2 pictures The child had come from Firozabad to her maternal grandfather's house Saurabh lives in Sariya village, in the Sirsaganj police station area of Firozabad district. His 4-year-old daughter, Bittu, had come to her maternal grandfather's house in Gopalpura village, Jaitpur area, Agra. On Thursday evening, around 4 PM, she was playing near the house. Suddenly, her foot slipped, and she fell into a deep well nearby. As soon as this was known, a large crowd of villagers gathered at the spot. People informed the police and administration. Firefighter Descended into Well with Oxygen Cylinder Upon receiving the information, police from several stations, including DCP Abhishek Agrawal, and a fire brigade team reached the spot. Due to poisonous gas and lack of oxygen in the well, initial rescue efforts faced difficulties. Subsequently, a firefighter descended into the well with an oxygen cylinder and safety equipment. After much effort, he was able to reach the child. The child was pulled out after about 4 hours. However, by then her condition had become extremely critical. When the child was taken to the hospital, doctors declared her dead. Father said- The oxygen cylinder took 3 hours to arrive After the child's death, father Saurabh's anger erupted at the scene. He expressed his displeasure by holding the hand of SDM Vinod Kumar. He said- The work that should have been done in one hour took three to four hours. If my daughter had been pulled out in time, she would have been with us today. He alleged that the fire brigade did not have adequate resources. It took about 3 hours for the oxygen cylinder to arrive. No speed was shown in the rescue either. Father said - Daughter was not given oxygen even in the ambulance Saurabh also accused the hospital administration of negligence. He said that the child was being sent to Agra for a post-mortem without informing them. There was no nurse in the ambulance, nor was his daughter given oxygen. He demanded action against the responsible officials in the entire matter and said that the family would soon file a written complaint.

The incident highlighted scrutiny of the board's evaluation process.

Ukraine receives new German IRIS-T air defence launcher amid continued Russian attacks

This latest delivery adds to previous transfers of the German-made medium-range surface-to-air missile system, which is crucial for protecting cities and infrastructure.

stories.title: From heatwave precautions to community service: PM Modi's top quotes from Mann Ki Baat
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi's Mann Ki Baat highlighted inspiring social service, water conservation, and sports achievements. The address emphasized citizen participation and recognizing ordinary Indians making extraordinary contributions to nation-building.

Banerjee claimed he was hit on the head with a stone and accused the police of inaction, calling it an attempt to murder.

stories.title: Israel captures strategic Lebanon castle after days of fighting despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli troops have captured the strategic Beaufort Castle in southern Lebanon, marking their deepest incursion in over 26 years. This territorial gain occurred despite an existing ceasefire, with forces advancing near Nabatiyeh to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure. The operation aims to eliminate perceived threats to Israeli civilians.

stories.title: Indian-origin Disney manager Jugal Daterao gets 2.5-year jail term in Russia over drug case
stories.summary: An Indian-origin Disney executive, Jugal Daterao, has received a two-and-a-half-year prison sentence in Russia for drug possession and smuggling. Authorities found THC-infused gummy candies in his luggage at a Moscow airport. Daterao claimed the gummies were legally prescribed in the US for post-brain surgery effects, but the court rejected his defense.

stories.title: 'You are arrogant': Mamata Banerjee heard scolding Kolkata hospital authorities
stories.summary: A video shows Mamata Banerjee confronting hospital officials in Kolkata, reportedly over her nephew Abhishek Banerjee's treatment after an alleged attack. BJP leaders criticised Banerjee, accusing her of pressuring the hospital despite reports of no major injuries. The incident follows an alleged stone-pelting attack on Abhishek Banerjee during a visit.

stories.title: Trump to kick off US 250th anniversary concert celebrations but without several artists who quit

Organizers Freedom 250 announced Trump's June 24 kick-off in Washington, D.C. Trump himself suggested replacing the departed performers with a "Make America Great Again Rally" for the nation's 250th anniversary.

stories.title: Truck carrying Afghan refugees from Pakistan overturns, killing 22
stories.summary: A tragic road accident in eastern Afghanistan claimed at least 22 lives, including 10 children and five women, as a truck carrying returning refugees overturned. Officials reported around 36 others injured. The incident, attributed to the driver reportedly falling asleep, highlights the perilous journeys of Afghans returning from Pakistan and Iran amidst increased expulsions.

stories.title: Pakistan hires US lobbying firm to advance strategic interests in Washington amid Iran war diplomacy push
stories.summary: Pakistan has hired a US lobbying firm, Ervin Graves Strategy Group, for a two-year contract worth $50,000 monthly. The firm will advocate for Pakistan's diplomatic, economic, and strategic interests in Washington, engaging with Congress, the executive branch, and policy institutions. This initiative aims to bolster Pakistan's standing as a US ally and its role in regional diplomacy.

He stated that even facing severe threats would not make him yield. The summons follows a series of legal challenges and a recent visit by Kolkata Police to his residence, which was described as routine.

A total of 45,255 BLOs have been deployed to carry out the revision process. “Nearly 75 per cent of the electors have to only sign on the required forms, and do not need any document for the SIR. No genuine citizen will face any difficulty during the SIR,” Gopalan told reporters.

stories.summary: Personnel from the Forest Department, Forest Protection Force, Social Forestry Department and other agencies have been deployed across the affected areas. Officials said efforts are continuing to bring the blaze under control and stop it from spreading further into dense forest zones. Authorities have appealed to residents to avoid activities that could spark fires and to immediately alert officials about any fire-related incidents.

"Yes, I can see that Samrat Choudhary, who has become the chief minister only recently, is quite excited. Let him get me evicted by force. stories.title: Greek man appears in court charged over alleged plot to spy on Iranian journalist in London

Decades of dedicated habitat restoration and targeted conservation efforts have seen its numbers rebound significantly. This success story offers a rare glimmer of hope for British wildlife amidst ongoing environmental challenges.

stories.title: 'India is powerful and modernising its military': US defence secretary Pete Hegseth

He highlighted New Delhi as a critical anchor for regional balance and praised its growing industrial capacity for high-end military operations. The US is pursuing co-production initiatives with India, including for Javelin munitions, to enhance collective readiness.

stories.title: Priority operation: India rushes to evacuate 13 ships out of 'volatile' Hormuz as Gulf crisis deepens
stories.summary: "A coordinated priority is prepared through which we try to get our ships out. stories.summary: The Supreme Court has raised serious concerns regarding the National Testing Agency's continual mishaps with paper leaks, indicating a troubling pattern of negligence. Why was HasanAbi subpoenaed by the US Treasury? Cuba trip controversy explained

Several thermal power plants are shut down, causing significant power cuts, especially in rural areas. The state is facing a substantial shortfall in power generation. Efforts are underway to secure additional electricity from other states and through power exchanges to meet the demand.

stories.title: 'I love Prime Minister Modi': Trump makes surprise live call during US embassy event in Delhi - video
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump made a surprise audio call during the US Embassy's 250th Independence Day celebrations in Delhi, expressing his admiration for PM Modi and calling him "great" and "my friend." Trump emphasized the close US-India relationship, stating India can count on the US "100%" and that the two nations have "never been closer".

stories.title: Britain’s anxious young adults struggle with modern workplace demands, warns UK govt advisor
stories.summary: A UK government advisor highlights challenges for young Britons entering the workforce. Rising anxiety, depression, and technology dependence are making adaptation difficult. The advisor suggests flexible work and mental health support can benefit the economy. This comes as youth inactivity, particularly among those not in education or employment, continues to grow.

stories.title: Eviction notice to Delhi Gymkhana: Elite club members plan legal battle against Centre’s order, seek ‘no dislocation’
stories.summary: Members of the Delhi Gymkhana Club are preparing to challenge a government order to vacate their Lutyens' Delhi property. Lakhs of tribals gather at Red Fort to demand removal of converted Muslims, Christians from ST list
stories.summary: Nearly 1.5 lakh tribal people from across India gathered at the Red Fort, demanding the removal of converted Muslims and Christians from the Scheduled Tribe category. Organized by the Janajati Suraksha Manch, the event aimed to build support for a constitutional amendment under Article 342 to de-list converted tribals.

stories.title: Falta repoll result 2026: BJP's Debangshu Panda wins with nearly 1.5 lakh votes, TMC’s Jahangir Khan restricted to 7k
stories.summary: BJP's Debangshu Panda secured a decisive victory in the Falta repoll, winning by over a lakh votes. The Election Commission ordered the repoll due to "severe electoral offences" during the initial April 29 polling. This high-stakes seat for TMC saw their candidate finish a distant fourth after withdrawing from campaigning but remaining on the ballot.

stories.title: NEET paper leak: Pune school principal shared questions for money, CBI tells court
stories.summary: A school principal, Manisha Sanjay Havaldar, was arrested by the CBI in connection with the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. She allegedly shared exam questions with students for money, conspiring with another lecturer. Havaldar admitted to sharing Physics questions and receiving payments, later deleting chats and burning notes.

The group, which gained traction discussing unemployment and exam leaks, saw its website taken down. Founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the government of suppression and claimed to have received death threats.

This comes after students and parents reported widespread technical glitches and confusion regarding re-evaluation fees. The move aims to ensure a smooth, reliable, and transparent system for students seeking to review their exam papers.

stories.title: Trump turnaround: Open the straits, close the war
stories.summary: A new understanding with Iran is emerging to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. This comes after weeks of military escalation. Iran denies commitments to give up uranium or unconditionally reopen the straits.

The system's credibility is shaken, while also impacting the aspirations of countless young individuals.

India highlighted its strategy to diversify energy sources for security amid global uncertainties.

stories.title: ‘Feared Ladakh would become another Manipur’: Sonam Wangchuk says recent MHA talks signal positive shift but trust deficit remains
stories.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk acknowledged a positive step in talks between Ladakh representatives and the Centre, but warned trust-building remains incomplete. He cited unresolved protest cases and institutional issues, fearing Ladakh could become "another Manipur" due to growing unrest. Wangchuk stressed that government intent will be judged by actions on these outstanding matters.

stories.title: Last rites of Twisha Sharma performed at Bhopal crematorium 12 days after her death
stories.summary: Twisha Sharma's funeral was held in Bhopal as her family continues to demand justice in the alleged dowry death case. Her husband, the prime accused, has been arrested and remanded to police custody.

stories.summary: Tragedy struck Karnataka's Uttara Kannada district on Sunday as at least eight individuals, predominantly women, lost their lives after being swept away while bathing in the Thatte Hakkalu river near Bhatkal. Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal AP Singh presented awards to outstanding performers. The officers will now join the Aircraft and Systems Testing Establishment.

stories.summary: Rubio said the wide range of areas in which both countries cooperate reflected the strength of ties between Washington and New Delhi. "The list of issues that we work together with India on, the breadth of scope of them, is what highlights the fact that India is an important strategic partner in the United States, one of our most important strategic partners in the world," Rubio said. Rubio also referred to the democratic values shared by both countries.

stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and external affairs minister S Jaishankar reaffirmed strong US-India strategic ties, highlighting cooperation in defence, trade, energy and technology. Rubio said US visa reforms were global, not India-specific, while condemning racist remarks against Indian Americans. Both leaders discussed energy security, Quad cooperation, trade negotiations, Iran tensions and India’s multi-alignment foreign policy approach.

Global oil markets are closely monitoring developments.

stories.summary: US President Donald Trump praised the Secret Service and law enforcement for their swift action in neutralizing a gunman near the White House. The suspect, identified as Nasire Best, was killed after firing at agents. Trump highlighted the incident's importance for future presidential security, referencing a previous security breach.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak: India issues travel advisory against three African countries
stories.summary: In light of the ongoing Ebola crisis, India has advised its citizens to reconsider any unnecessary travel plans to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a significant deal with Iran is nearing completion. This agreement aims to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end ongoing hostilities. stories.title: Taiwan detects Chinese military aircraft, naval vessels near island for second straight day
stories.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported Chinese military activity, with four aircraft and six naval vessels detected around the island. Three aircraft crossed the Taiwan Strait median line. This follows a day of heightened activity, with 16 aircraft and eight vessels observed, 13 of which crossed the median line. These incursions underscore rising regional tensions.

stories.title: White House shooting: 21-year-old Nasire Best, who identified himself as Jesus Christ, shot dead
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man, Nasire Best, who allegedly believed he was Jesus Christ, was killed by Secret Service after opening fire outside the White House. Best had a history of loitering and violating orders to stay away from the complex. The incident triggered a lockdown and injured at least one bystander.

stories.title: '94% audience from India': Cockroach Janta Party founder rejects BJP's Pakistani-followers charge
stories.summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke refutes BJP claims of Pakistani followers. He presented audience analytics showing over 94% Indian users. Union minister Kiren Rijiju and BJP leader Sukanta Majumdar had alleged significant Pakistani engagement. Kerala BJP president Rajeev Chandrasekhar called it a cross-border influence operation. The party gained traction online discussing unemployment and policy issues.

stories.title: Iran agrees to give up enriched uranium as deal with Trump 'largely negotiated': Report
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly agreed in principle to surrender its enriched uranium stockpile to the US as part of a peace deal. While a deal is "largely negotiated," final details on the uranium transfer and broader nuclear talks are pending.

stories.summary: The gulf between Trump’s actions and Gabbard’s worldview made the latter’s position untenable. The post appeared shortly before the US struck Iran’s nuclear sites in an operation almost borrowed from the plot of Top Gun: Maverick.
